original: The sound is going away. Let’s follow it, and after do  our work.
translation: The sound is going away. Let’s follow it, and complete our plan after that.

original: Lead, monster; we’ll follow. I would I could see this  taborer. He lays it on.
translation: Lead on, monster. We’ll follow. I wish I could see this drummer. He's very good.

original: Wilt come? I’ll follow, Stephano.
translation: Coming, monster? I’m right behind you, Stephano.

original: [to ALONSO]   By 'r lakin, I can go no further, sir.   My old bones ache.
translation: [To ALONSO]  I swear on the Virgin Mary, I can’t go any further, sir. My old bones are aching.

original: Here’s a maze trod indeed   Through forthrights and meanders. By your patience,   I needs must rest me.
translation: It's like we're walking in a maze, with some paths straight and some crooked. If it's all right with you, I need to rest.

original: Old lord, I cannot blame thee,   Who am myself attached with weariness   To th' dulling of my spirits. Sit down and rest.
translation: Old lord, I can’t blame you, since I’m so tired that I'm becoming sad. Sit down and rest.

original: Even here I will put off my hope and keep it   No longer for my flatterer.
translation: In this spot I'm going to give up all hope.

original: He is drowned   Whom thus we stray to find, and the sea mocks   Our frustrate search on land. Well, let him go.
translation: The one whom we're trying to find—and getting ourselves lost in the process—is drowned.  The sea is laughing at us as we search for him on land. It's time to let him go.

original: I am right glad that he’s so out  of hope. Do not, for one repulse, forego the purpose That you resolved t' effect.
translation: I’m very glad he’s lost all hope. Don’t give up on the plan we agreed to carry out just because we failed in our first attempt.

original: The next advantage Will we take throughly.
translation: When we get another opportunity, we'll take it.

original: [aside to SEBASTIAN]   Let it be tonight,   For now they are oppressed with travel.
translation: [To SEBASTIAN so that only he can hear]  Let’s do it tonight, because the men are so exhausted from traveling.

original: They   Will not, nor cannot, use such vigilance   As when they are fresh.
translation: They won't, or can't, be as careful as they are when they have more energy.

original: I say, tonight. No more.
translation: Agreed. Tonight it is. Now be quiet.

original: What harmony is this? My good friends, hark!
translation: What is that music? My good friends, listen!

original: Marvelous sweet music!
translation: What marvelous, beautiful music!

original: Give us kind keepers, heavens! What were these?
translation: May your angels protect us, heaven! What were those things?

original: A living drollery. Now I will believe   That there are unicorns,
translation: A puppet show with living actors. Now that I've seen that, I’ll believe that unicorns exist,

original: that in Arabia   There is one tree, the phoenix' throne, one phoenix   At this hour reigning there.
translation: and that there’s a tree in Arabia where the phoenix lives, with a phoenix sitting in it right now.

original: I’ll believe both   And what does else want credit, come to me,   And I’ll be sworn ’tis true.
translation: I'll believe both those things too. And if there's anything else that seems like it can't be real, just come to me and I’ll swear it’s true.

original: Travelers ne'er did lie,   Though fools at home condemn 'em.
translation: Travelers have never told lies, even if fools back home accuse them of making things up.

original: If in Naples   I should report this now, would they believe me?   If I should say, I saw such islanders—   For, certes, these are people of the island—
translation: If I described this back in Naples, would they believe me? Would they believe it if I told them that I saw native islanders such as these— because they must certainly be natives of the island—

original: Who, though they are of monstrous shape, yet note,   Their manners are more gentle-kind than of   Our human generation you shall find   Many—nay, almost any.
translation: who despite their unnatural shape have more grace and better manners than you can find among many—actually, almost any—human beings?

original: Honest lord, Thou hast said well, for some of you there present Are worse than devils.
translation: You honest lord, what you've said is true, since some of you right there are worse than devils.

original: I cannot too much muse   Such shapes, such gesture, and such sound, expressing,
translation: I can’t stop wondering about those shapes and their movements and sounds, which expressed—

original: Although they want the use of tongue, a kind   Of excellent dumb discourse.
translation: even without being able to speak—a kind of incredible mute language.

original: Praise in departing.
translation: Don't offer your praise until you've seen the whole performance.

original: They vanished strangely.
translation: They disappeared in a strange way.

original: No matter, since They have left their viands behind, for we have  stomachs. Will ’t please you taste of what is here?
translation: It doesn't matter, since they left their food behind, and we have hungry stomachs. Would you like to taste some of the food?

original: Not I.
translation: Not me.

original: Faith, sir, you need not fear. When we were boys,   Who would believe that there were mountaineers   Dewlapped like bulls, whose throats had hanging at 'em   Wallets of flesh,
translation: I promise you, sir, you have nothing to fear. When we were boys, who would have believed that there were people who lived in the mountains that had pouches of skin hanging down from their necks, as  cattle  do?

original: or that there were such men   Whose heads stood in their breasts?—which now we find   Each putter-out of five for one will bring us   Good warrant of.
translation: Or that there were men who had  their heads in their chests ? And now every traveler returns with word that such things are real.

original: I will stand to and feed,   Although my last.   No matter,
translation: I’ll take the risk and eat. Even if this turns out to be my last meal, that's all right,

original: since I feel   The best is past. Brother, my lord the duke,   Stand to and do as we.
translation: since I know the best part of my life is in the past. Brother, my lord Duke, please have some food as well.

original: [to ALONSO, ANTONIO, and SEBASTIAN]   You are three men of sin, whom Destiny,   That hath to instrument this lower world   And what is in ’t, the never-surfeited sea   Hath caused to belch up you—
translation: [To ALONSO, ANTONIO, andSEBASTIAN]  The three of you are sinners. Destiny—which controls the earth and everything in it—caused the sea to throw you up onto

original: and on this island   Where man doth not inhabit, you ’mongst men   Being most unfit to live. I have made you mad,   And even with suchlike valor men hang and drown   Their proper selves.
translation: this uninhabited island, because you are unfit to live among other people. I have driven you crazy, and men with the reckless courage given by insanity often hang or drown themselves.

original: [ALONSO, SEBASTIAN, and ANTONIO draw their swords]   You fools, I and my fellows   Are ministers of fate.
translation: [ALONSO, SEBASTIAN, and ANTONIO draw their swords]  You fools, my fellow harpies and I are the agents of Fate.

original: The elements   Of whom your swords are tempered may as well   Wound the loud winds or with bemocked-at stabs   Kill the still-closing waters as diminish   One dowl that’s in my plume.
translation: Your swords would be no more useful for injuring the whistling winds or stabbing the water—always closing up around the hole your sword makes in it—than they would be for cutting off even one of my feathers.

original: My fellow ministers   Are like invulnerable. If you could hurt,   Your swords are now too massy for your strengths   And will not be uplifted. But remember—
translation: My comrades are just as indestructible. And even if you could hurt us, I’ve made your swords too heavy for you to lift. But remember—

original: For that’s my business to you—that you three   From Milan did supplant good Prospero,   Exposed unto the sea, which hath requit it,   Him and his innocent child.
translation: because reminding you of this is why I’m here—that in Milan the three of you overthrew Prospero, and abandoned him in the ocean with his innocent child.

original: For which foul deed   The powers—delaying, not forgetting—have   Incensed the seas and shores, yea, all the creatures,   Against your peace.
translation: Now the ocean has paid you back for your evil actions. The gods—delaying their punishment, not forgetting it—have raised up the seas, the land, and every creature against you and any hope you may have had of peace.

original: Thee of thy son, Alonso,   They have bereft, and do pronounce by me   Lingering perdition, worse than any death   Can be at once, shall step by step attend   You and your ways;
translation: From you, Alonso, they’ve taken your son, and have commanded that I inflict upon you a slow ruin that follows you step-by-step, and is worse than a quick death.

original: whose wraths to guard you from—   Which here, in this most desolate isle, else falls   Upon your heads—is nothing but hearts' sorrow   And a clear life ensuing.
translation: The only way to protect yourself from the anger of the gods—which here, on this deserted island, will otherwise fall on your heads—is for you to feel truly sorry in your heart for what you’ve done, and from now on to live good and moral lives.

original: [aside]   Bravely the figure of this harpy hast thou   Performed, my Ariel. A grace it had, devouring.   Of my instruction hast thou nothing bated   In what thou hadst to say.
translation: [To himself]  You’ve put on a great show of being a harpy, my Ariel. The performance had grace, and yet also a fierce consuming power. You followed my instructions and left out nothing that I asked you to say.

original: So with good life   And observation strange, my meaner ministers   Their several kinds have done.
translation: With a unique attention to detail, even my less powerful servants have performed their different roles with excellent realism.

original: My high charms work   And these mine enemies are all knit up   In their distractions.
translation: My magic spells are working, and my enemies are all caught up in their bewilderment.

original: They now are in my power,   And in these fits I leave them while I visit   Young Ferdinand, whom they suppose is drowned,   And his and mine loved darling.
translation: They are now under my control, and I'll leave them stuck here in their confusion while I visit young Ferdinand—whom they think has drowned—and the darling girl both he and I love.

original: I' th' name of something holy, sir, why  stand you In this strange stare?
translation: In the name of all that is holy, sir, why do you stand there staring strangely around?

original: Oh, it is monstrous, monstrous.   Methought the billows spoke and told me of it,   The winds did sing it to me, and the thunder,   That deep and dreadful organ pipe,
translation: Oh, it’s awful, awful. I thought the clouds spoke to me; the winds sang to me; and the thunder roared like the deep and terrible sound of an organ—all of them

original: pronounced   The name of Prosper. It did bass my trespass.   Therefore my son i' th' ooze is bedded,
translation: said the name of Prospero.  Singing in a deep note, the voice spoke of the bad things I've done, and told me that, because of what I did, my son now sleeps on the ocean floor.

original: and   I’ll seek him deeper than e'er plummet sounded   And with him there lie mudded.
translation: Now I'll go search for him deeper than an anchor has ever sank, and lie with him in the mud.

original: But one fiend at a time, I’ll fight their legions o'er.
translation: I’ll fight their entire army of devils, one at a time.

original: I’ll be thy second.
translation: I’ll support you.

original: All three of them are desperate. Their great guilt,   Like poison given to work a great time after,   Now 'gins to bite the spirits.
translation: All three of them are desperate. Their guilt—like a poison given time to work in their bodies—now begins to bite at their consciences.

original: I do beseech you   That are of suppler joints, follow them swiftly   And hinder them from what this ecstasy   May now provoke them to.
translation: Those who are lively and energetic, I beg you, quickly follow them and stop them from doing whatever this fit of insanity is pushing them to do.

original: Follow, I pray you.
translation: Follow them, please.

original: [to FERDINAND]   If I have too austerely punished you,   Your compensation makes amends, for I   Have given you here a third of mine own life—   Or that for which I live—
translation: [To FERDINAND]  If I’ve been too strict in my punishment of you, your compensation will make it better. For I am giving you my daughter, who makes up a third of my entire life, and who is everything I live for.

original: who once again   I tender to thy hand. All thy vexations   Were but my trials of thy love and thou   Hast strangely stood the test.
translation: I put her into your hands. All of the trouble I gave you was just my way of testing your love for her, and you have endured those tests extraordinarily well.

original: Here, afore heaven,   I ratify this my rich gift. O Ferdinand,   Do not smile at me that I boast of her,   For thou shalt find she will outstrip all praise   And make it halt behind her.
translation: Here, before God, I promise you that I will give you this precious gift. Oh, Ferdinand, don’t laugh at me for praising her so highly, because you’ll discover that she exceeds all the praise given to her.

original: I do believe it Against an oracle.
Then as my gift and thine own acquisition   Worthily purchased, take my daughter.
translation: Then, as a gift from me and as your well-earned reward, take my daughter.

original: But   If thou dost break her virgin knot before   All sanctimonious ceremonies may   With full and holy rite be ministered,
translation: But if you take her virginity before the marriage ceremony is performed according to all the sacred traditions,

original: No sweet aspersion shall the heavens let fall   To make this contract grow, but barren hate,   Sour-eyed disdain,
translation: the heavens will not shower blessings on your marriage. Instead, empty hate, bitter disrespect,

original: and discord shall bestrew   The union of your bed with weeds so loathly   That you shall hate it both.
translation: and conflict will ruin your marriage until you both grow to despise it.

original: Therefore take heed,   As Hymen’s lamps shall light you.
translation: So listen to what I'm saying if you want to have a happy marriage blessed by  Hymen .

original: As I hope   For quiet days, fair issue, and long life,   With such love as ’tis now,
translation: Since I hope to enjoy quiet days, beautiful children, and a long life filled with the love that I have now,

original: the murkiest den,   The most opportune place, the strong’st suggestion,   Our worser genius can shall never melt   Mine honor into lust to take away   The edge of that day’s celebration
translation: not even the greatest opportunity or strongest temptation will allow my worse instincts to overcome my honor, and let me give in to lust. Doing so would only remove the anticipation from that day's celebration,

original: When I shall think, or Phoebus' steeds are foundered,   Or night kept chained below.
translation: when I'll be so excited for my first night with Miranda that I'll wonder if the  sun  has stopped in the sky, or if night has been locked away somehow.

original: Fairly spoke. Sit then and talk with her. She is thine own. What, Ariel! My industrious servant, Ariel!
translation: Well said. Sit then, and talk with her. She is yours. Come here, Ariel! My busy servant, Ariel!

original: What would my potent master? Here I am.
translation: What would my mighty master like? I am here.

original: Thou and thy meaner fellows your last service   Did worthily perform, and I must use you   In such another trick.
translation: You and your lesser friends performed well in your last task, and now I need you to do something similar.

original: Go bring the rabble,   O'er whom I give thee power, here to this place.
translation: Go bring the whole group here. I give you the power to control them.

original: Incite them to quick motion, for I must   Bestow upon the eyes of this young couple   Some vanity of mine art. It is my promise,   And they expect it from me.
translation: Make sure they come quickly, because I must use my magic to give this young couple a show. I promised I would, and they’re expecting it.

original: Presently?
translation: Immediately?

original: Ay, with a twink.
translation: Yes, in the twinkling of an eye.

original: Before you can say “Come” and “Go,”   And breathe twice and cry “So, so!”
translation: Before you can say “Come” and “Go"—and breathe twice and shout “So, so!"—

original: Each one, tripping on his toe,   Will be here with mop and mow.   Do you love me, master, no?
translation: each one of your servants, leaping on their toes, will arrive here with their gestures and silly faces. Do you love me, master? No?

original: Dearly my delicate Ariel. Do not approach Till thou dost hear me call.
translation: Dearly, my lovely Ariel. Don’t come until you hear me call for you.

original: Well, I conceive.
translation: Yes, I understand.

original: [to FERDINAND]   Look thou be true. Do not give dalliance   Too much the rein.
translation: [To FERDINAND]  Be mindful that you stay true to your promise to remain chaste before marriage. Don’t let your flirting push you over the edge.

original: The strongest oaths are straw   To th' fire i' th' blood. Be more abstemious,   Or else, goodnight your vow.
translation: Even the strongest promises can get burned to a crisp by the fire of lust in your blood. Be more self-disciplined, or else say goodbye to your vow.

original: I warrant you, sir, The white cold virgin snow upon my heart Abates the ardor of my liver.
Well.   Now come, my Ariel!
translation: Good. Now come, my Ariel!

original: Bring a corollary,   Rather than want a spirit. Appear and pertly!—   No tongue. All eyes! Be silent.
translation: It's better to bring an extra helper along than to need a spirit and not have one. Appear, quickly! No talking. Watch! Be quiet.

original: Ceres, most bounteous lady, thy rich leas   Of wheat, rye, barley, vetches, oats, and peas;   Thy turfy mountains, where live nibbling sheep,   And flat meads thatched with stover, them to keep;
translation: Ceres , I am the messenger that carries the rainbow for  Juno , the Queen of the Sky. She commands you to leave behind your rich farmlands of wheat, rye, barley, oats, and peas; the grassy hills where sheep graze and the meadows covered with hay for the sheep to eat in winter;

original: Thy banks with pionèd and twillèd brims,   Which spongy April at thy hest betrims   To make cold nymphs chaste crowns; and thy broom  groves,
translation: your riverbanks covered in vines and branches that April, on your orders, covers with flowers for virginal nymphs to use to make crowns; your yellow-flowered groves

original: Whose shadow the dismissèd bachelor loves,   Being lass-lorn; thy pole-clipped vineyard;   And thy sea-marge, sterile and rocky hard,   Where thou thyself dost air—
translation: where young men go when they have been rejected by their lovers; your pruned vineyards; your rocky seashore where you yourself fly.

original: the Queen o' th' Sky,   Whose watery arch and messenger am I,   Bids thee leave these, and with her sovereign grace,   Here on this grass plot, in this very place,   To come and sport. Her peacocks fly amain.
translation: Leave all those places, and come to meet the Queen on this grassy spot—this very place—to come and play. The peacocks that draw her chariot approach at full speed.

original: Approach, rich Ceres, her to entertain.
translation: Come, rich Ceres, and entertain Juno.

original: Hail, many-colored messenger, that ne'er   Dost disobey the wife of Jupiter;   Who with thy saffron wings upon my flowers   Diffusest honey drops, refreshing showers;
translation: Hello, many-colored messenger, who never disobeys Juno, the wife of Jupiter. With your golden wings you scatter dewdrops—those refreshing showers—on my flowers.

original: And with each end of thy blue bow dost crown   My bosky acres and my unshrubbed down,   Rich scarf to my proud earth. Why hath thy queen   Summoned me hither to this short-grassed green?
translation: You crown my woodlands and fields with each end of your rainbow, making a gorgeous scarf for my delighted earth. Why has your queen summoned me here to this grassy place?

original: A contract of true love to celebrate, And some donation freely to estate On the blessed lovers.
translation: To celebrate a marriage of true love, and to give a gift to the blessed lovers.

original: Tell me, heavenly bow,   If Venus or her son, as thou dost know,   Do now attend the queen?
translation: Tell me, heavenly rainbow, do you know if either  Venus  or her son Cupid are with the queen?

original: Since they did plot   The means that dusky Dis my daughter got,   Her and her blind boy’s scandaled company   I have forsworn.
translation: Ever since the two of them plotted a way for  Dis  to steal from me my daughter Proserpina, I have sworn never to go near Venus or her blind son again.

original: Of her society   Be not afraid. I met her deity   Cutting the clouds towards Paphos, and her son   Dove-drawn with her.
translation: Don’t be afraid that you will have to see her. I met Venus as she was flying with her son in a carriage pulled by doves through the sky towards her home on the island of Paphos.

original: Here thought they to have done   Some wanton charm upon this man and maid,   Whose vows are that no bed-right shall be paid   Till Hymen’s torch be lighted—but in vain.
translation: They had been planning to put a magic spell upon this man and woman. The spell would have made them break their vow that they would not sleep together until Hymen's torch was lit on their wedding day.

original: Mars’s hot minion is returned again.   Her waspish-headed son has broke his arrows,   Swears he will shoot no more, but play with sparrows   And be a boy right out.
translation: Venus, that lustful wife of Mars, has returned home again. And hot-headed Cupid has broken all his arrows. He swears he will never shoot them again, and will instead play with sparrows like a regular boy.

original: Highest queen of state, Great Juno, comes. I know her by her gait.
translation: The most powerful queen, Great Juno, comes. I know her by her walk.

original: How does my bounteous sister? Go with me To bless this twain that they may prosperous be, And honored in their issue.
translation: How is my generous sister? Come with me to bless this couple so they will be successful, and have wonderful children.

original: Honor, riches, marriage, blessing,   Long continuance, and increasing,
translation: May honor, riches, marriage, blessings,  Long life, and ever increasing,

original: Hourly joys be still upon you.   Juno sings her blessings on you.
translation: Constant joy be always with you.  Juno sings her blessings to you.

original: Earth’s increase, foison plenty,   Barns and garners never empty,   Vines and clustering bunches growing,   Plants with goodly burden bowing—
translation: The blessings of earth, plentiful harvests,  Always full barns and silos,  Vines full of clustered grapes,  Plants bending under the weight of their fruit—

original: Spring come to you at the farthest   In the very end of harvest.
translation: May spring follow Right after the end of autumn’s harvest.

original: Scarcity and want shall shun you.   Ceres' blessing so is on you.
translation: Lack and poverty will never touch you.  That is Ceres’ blessing for you.

original: This is a most majestic vision, and   Harmonious charmingly.
translation: This show is an incredible illusion, with enchantingly harmonious music.

original: May I be bold   To think these spirits?
translation: Am I right to think that these are spirits that we're watching?

original: Spirits, which by mine art I have from their confines called to enact My present fancies.
translation: They are spirits that I've called out from their dwellings to perform my current fantasy, all through my magic.

original: Let me live here ever. So rare a wondered father and a wife Makes this place paradise.
translation: Let me live here forever. Such a wonderful father-in-law and wife make this place a paradise.

original: Sweet now, silence.   Juno and Ceres whisper seriously.
translation: [To MIRANDA, who is about to speak]  Quiet for now, darling. Juno and Ceres are whispering about something serious.

original: There’s something else to do. Hush and be mute,   Or else our spell is marred.
translation: There’s something else they must do. Be quiet and don't speak, or else my spell will be broken.

original: You nymphs, called Naiads of the windring brooks,   With your sedged crowns and ever-harmless looks,
translation: You nymphs, called Naiads, who live in the wandering streams! With your crowns of grass and always innocent looks,

original: Leave your crisp channels and on this green land   Answer your summons, Juno does command.
translation: leave your cool streams and obey Juno's command. Come up on this grassy field. Juno orders you.

original: Come, temperate nymphs, and help to celebrate   A contract of true love. Be not too late.
translation: Come, chaste nymphs, and help us celebrate the engagement of two true lovers. Don’t be late.

original: You   sunburnt sicklemen of August weary,   Come hither from the furrow and be merry.   Make holiday.
translation: Now, you sunburned farmers—so tired from all the work you must do in August—come here from your rows of planting and have fun. Celebrate.

original: Your rye-straw hats put on,   And these fresh nymphs encounter every one   In country footing.
translation: Put on your straw hats and dance with these young nymphs.

original: I had forgot that foul conspiracy   Of the beast Caliban and his confederates   Against my life.
translation: I forgot about Caliban’s evil conspiracy with his companions to kill me.

original: The minute of their plot   Is almost come.—
translation: The time for them to act on their plot is almost here.

original: Well done. Avoid, no more!
translation: [To the spirits]  Well done. Now leave, no more!

original: This is strange. Your father’s in some  passion That works him strongly.
translation: This is strange. Some strong feeling has deeply upset your father.

original: Never till this day Saw I him touched with anger so distempered.
translation: I’ve never in my life seen him this angry and upset.

original: [to FERDINAND]   You do look, my son, in a moved sort,   As if you were dismayed. Be cheerful, sir.   Our revels now are ended.
translation: [To FERDINAND]  My son-in-law, you look troubled, as if something has made you upset. Cheer up, sir. The show is now finished.

original: These our actors,   As I foretold you, were all spirits and   Are melted into air, into thin air.
translation: These actors, as I told you, were all spirits, and they’ve melted into the air, thin air.

original: And like the baseless fabric of this vision,   The cloud-capped towers, the gorgeous palaces,   The solemn temples,
translation: And like this vision—with its towers reaching to the clouds, its gorgeous palaces, its grand temples (which in fact have no underlying structure)—

original: the great globe itself,   Ye all which it inherit, shall dissolve,   And like this insubstantial pageant faded,   Leave not a rack behind.
translation: the actual world, and everyone living in it, will dissolve just as this illusion has disappeared, leaving not even a wisp of cloud behind.

original: We are such stuff   As dreams are made on, and our little life   Is rounded with a sleep. Sir, I am vexed.
translation: We are all made of the stuff of dreams, and our small lifespans stretch from the sleep before birth to the sleep after death. Sir, I’m upset.

original: Bear with my weakness. My old brain is troubled.   Be not disturbed with my infirmity.
translation: Please put up with this weakness of mine. My old brain is troubled, but don’t be disturbed by it.

original: If you be pleased, retire into my cell   And there repose. A turn or two I’ll walk   To still my beating mind.
translation: If you would like to, you can go to my hut and relax. I’ll take a little walk to calm my restless mind.

original: We wish your peace.
translation: We hope you find some peace.

original: Come with a thought. I thank thee, Ariel. Come.
translation: Ariel—I call you with a thought. I thank you, Ariel. Come.

original: Thy thoughts I cleave to. What’s thy pleasure?
translation: I follow all your thoughts. What do you want?

original: Spirit, We must prepare to meet with Caliban.
translation: Spirit, we must prepare to deal with Caliban.

original: Ay, my commander. When I presented Ceres, I thought to have told thee of it, but I feared Lest I might anger thee.
translation: Yes, my leader. When I was presenting the show about Ceres, I thought of mentioning Caliban to you, but I was afraid I might make you angry.

original: Say again, where didst thou leave these varlets?
translation: Tell me again, where did you leave those villains?

original: I told you, sir, they were red-hot with drinking,   So full of valor that they smote the air   For breathing in their faces, beat the ground   For kissing of their feet;
translation: I told you, sir, they were wildly drunk—so full of inflated courage that they were striking at the air with their swords for blowing in their faces, and hitting the ground for touching their feet.

original: yet always bending   Towards their project. Then I beat my tabor,   At which, like unbacked colts, they pricked their ears,   Advanced their eyelids, lifted up their noses   As they smelt music.
translation: Yet at the same time they’ve never lost sight of their plan. Then I beat my drum, at which—like colts that had never been ridden—they pricked up their ears, looked around, and lifted their noises as if to smell the music.

original: So I charmed their ears   That, calflike, they my lowing followed through   Toothed briers, sharp furzes, pricking gorse, and  thorns,   Which entered their frail shins.
translation: So with my music I put a spell on their ears that made them follow me like trusting calves through sharp-leaved bushes, prickly shrubs, and thorns—all of which stuck in their vulnerable shins.

original: At last I left them   I' th' filthy-mantled pool beyond your cell,   There dancing up to th' chins, that the foul lake   O'erstunk their feet.
translation: Finally, I left them in the middle of the scum-covered pond behind your hut, with the stinking water lapping at their chins.

original: This was well done, my bird.   Thy shape invisible retain thou still.
translation: That was well done, my little friend. Remain invisible.

original: The trumpery in my house, go bring it hither   For stale to catch these thieves.
translation: Go get those cheap, showy clothes from my house. Bring them here for us to use as bait to catch these thieves.

original: I go, I go.
translation: Here I go, here I go.

original: A devil, a born devil on whose nature   Nurture can never stick, on whom my pains,   Humanely taken, all, all lost, quite lost.
translation: He's a devil, a devil from the moment he was born. His nature can never be changed, no matter how much care he receives. All my work for him—all done with sincere care for him—had no effect, absolutely no effect.

original: And as with age his body uglier grows,   So his mind cankers. I will plague them all,   Even to roaring.
translation: As he grows older, his body grows uglier, and his mind becomes more evil. I’ll put them all in agony until they roar in pain.

original: Come, hang them on this line.
translation: Come here. Hang these clothes on this clothesline.

original: Pray you, tread softly, that the blind mole may not  hear a foot fall. We now are near his cell.
translation: Please, walk quietly, so that not even a blind mole would hear our feet touch the ground. We are now near his hut.

original: Monster, your fairy, which you say is a harmless fairy, has done little better than played the jack with us.
translation: Hey, monster, that spirit—who you said is harmless—has done nothing but play prank after prank on us.

original: Monster, I do smell all horse piss, at which my nose is in great indignation.
translation: Monster, I smell like horse piss, and my nose is not at all happy about it.

original: So is mine. Do you hear, monster? If I should take a  displeasure against you, look you—
translation: Mine too. Do you hear what I'm saying, monster? If I become unhappy with you, be careful—

original: Thou wert but a lost monster.
translation: You’d be a lost monster.

original: Good my lord, give me thy favor still.   Be patient, for the prize I’ll bring thee to   Shall hoodwink this mischance.
translation: My good lord, don't give up on me. Be patient, because the prize I’m bringing you to will cover up the bad luck we had before.

original: Therefore speak softly.   All’s hushed as midnight yet.
translation: So please speak quietly. Everything's quiet, as if it's the middle of the night.

original: Ay, but to lose our bottles in the pool—
translation: All right. But I'm not happy that we lost our wine bottles in the pond—

original: There is not only disgrace and dishonor in that,  monster, but an infinite loss.
translation: Monster, losing those bottles of wine was a loss much worse than disgrace or dishonor.

original: That’s more to me than my wetting. Yet this is your  harmless fairy, monster.
translation: I'm angrier about losing them than I am about having gotten wet. Yet you said the spirit was harmless, monster.

original: I will fetch off my bottle, though I be o'er ears for  my labor.
translation: I’ll get my bottle of wine back, even if it means I have to go down into that pond so the water is over my ears.

original: Prithee, my king, be quiet. Seest thou here,   This is the mouth o' th' cell. No noise, and enter.
translation: Please, my king, be quiet. Do you see this? It's the door to his hut. Be silent and enter.

original: Do that good mischief which may make this island   Thine own for ever, and I, thy Caliban,   For aye thy foot-licker.
translation: Commit the good crime that will make this island yours forever. And I, your Caliban, will always be your worshipful foot-licker.

original: Give me thy hand. I do begin to have bloody thoughts.
translation: Give me your hand. I’m starting to want to spill some blood.

original: O King Stephano! O peer, O worthy Stephano, look what a wardrobe here is for thee!
translation: Oh, King Stephano! Oh, worthy Stephano, look at the clothes hanging here for you!

original: Let it alone, thou fool. It is but trash.
translation: Ignore it, you fool. It’s trash.

original: Oh, ho, monster, we know what belongs to a frippery.—     O King Stephano!
translation: Oh, right, monster, we know what sort of clothes are nothing more than second-hand rags. And these are good quality.  Oh, King Stephano!

original: Put off that gown, Trinculo. By this hand, I’ll have  that gown.
translation: Take off that gown, Trinculo. Give me that gown, or I swear by my hand, I will beat you up.

original: Thy grace shall have it.
The dropsy drown this fool! What do you mean   To dote thus on such luggage? Let’s alone,   And do the murder first.
translation: May this fool die of a heart attack! Why are you obsessing over this junk? Leave the clothes alone, and let's commit the murder first.

original: If he awake,   From toe to crown he’ll fill our skins with pinches,   Make us strange stuff.
translation: If Prospero wakes up, he’ll torment us from head to foot and transform us into something awful.

original: Be you quiet, monster.—Mistress line, is not this my  jerkin? Now is the jerkin under the line.—Now, jerkin,  you are like to lose your hair and prove a bald jerkin.
Do, do. We steal by line and level, an ’t like your  grace.
translation: Do it, do it. We’re stealing with a plumb-line and carpenter's level, like real professionals, if it please your Grace.

original: I thank thee for that jest. Here’s a garment for ’t.  Wit shall not go unrewarded while I am king of this  country. “Steal by line and level” is an excellent pass  of pate. There’s another garment for ’t.
translation: Thanks for that joke. Here's some clothes in return. Jokes won't go unrewarded when I'm king of this country. “Stealing with a plumb-line and carpenter's level” is an excellent little joke. Here’s some more clothes as a reward.

original: Monster, come, put some lime upon your fingers, and  away with the rest.
I will have none on ’t. We shall lose our time, And all be turned to barnacles or to apes With foreheads villainous low.
translation: I won’t be a part of this. We’ll miss our opportunity and we'll all get turned into geese or apes with wretchedly low foreheads.

original: Monster, lay to your fingers. Help to bear this away  where my hogshead of wine is, or I’ll turn you out of my kingdom. Go to, carry this.
translation: Monster, use your fingers. Help to carry these clothes to where my barrel of wine is, or I’ll throw you out of my kingdom. Get going, carry this.

original: And this.
translation: And this.

original: Ay, and this.
translation: Yes, and this.

original: Hey, Mountain, hey!
translation: Hey, Mountain, hey!

original: Silver. There it goes, Silver!
translation: Silver. Follow them, Silver!

original: Fury, Fury! There, Tyrant, there. Hark, hark!
translation: Fury, Fury! Over there, Tyrant, there. Look, look!

original: Go charge my goblins that they grind their joints   With dry convulsions,
translation: Ariel, go tell my goblin servants to make their joints shake with convulsions,

original: shorten up their sinews   With agèd cramps, and more pinch-spotted make them   Than pard or cat o' mountain.
translation: to make them double over with cramps, and cover them bruises so that they have more spots than a leopard or wildcat.

original: Hark, they roar.
translation: Listen, they’re roaring in pain.

original: Let them be hunted soundly. At this hour   Lie at my mercy all mine enemies.
translation: May they be hunted down. As of now, all my enemies are at my mercy.

original: Shortly shall all my labors end, and thou   Shalt have the air at freedom. For a little   Follow, and do me service.
translation: Soon all my work will be done, and you’ll be free to fly wherever you want. For a little longer, though, follow my orders and do some more work for me.

original: Now does my project gather to a head.
translation: Now my plan is coming to its conclusion.

original: My charms crack not, my spirits obey, and time   Goes upright with his carriage. How’s the day?
translation: My spells are not breaking, my spirits are obeying me, and everything is running smoothly. What time is it?

original: On the sixth hour, at which time, my lord, You said our work should cease.
translation: It’s nearly six o'clock, my lord, which is when you said our work would be done.

original: I did say so   When first I raised the tempest.
translation: I did say that what I first created the storm at sea.

original: Say, my spirit,   How fares the king and ’s followers?
translation: Tell me, my spirit, how are the king and his followers?

original: Confined together   In the same fashion as you gave in charge,   Just as you left them, all prisoners, sir,   In the line grove which weather-fends your cell.
translation: Locked up together—exactly as you commanded and just as you left them. Sir, they are prisoners in the grove of lime trees that shields your hut from bad weather.

original: They cannot budge till your release. The king,   His brother, and yours, abide all three distracted,   And the remainder mourning over them,   Brimful of sorrow and dismay.
translation: They can’t budge until you release them. The king, his brother, and your brother are waiting, out of their wits. Everyone else is worried about them, and completely shocked and sad.

original: But chiefly   Him that you termed, sir, “the good old Lord Gonzalo,”   His tears run down his beard like winter’s drops   From eaves of reeds.
translation: The one you called “the good old lord Gonzalo” is the most upset. Tears run down his beard like melting snow from a thatched roof.

original: Your charm so strongly works 'em   That if you now beheld them, your affections   Would become tender.
translation: Your magic has affected them so deeply that if you saw them now, you’d feel bad for them.

original: Dost thou think so, spirit?
translation: Do you think so, spirit?

original: Mine would, sir, were I human.
translation: I would, sir, if I were human.

original: And mine shall.   Hast thou, which art but air, a touch, a feeling   Of their afflictions, and shall not myself,   One of their kind, that relish all as sharply   Passion as they, be kindlier moved than thou art?
translation: As will I. If you, made of air, can feel slightly sorry for them, then I, a human like them who has experienced all the feelings they have, will be even more affected than you.

original: Though with their high wrongs I am struck to th' quick,   Yet with my nobler reason 'gainst my fury   Do I take part.
translation: Though I’m furious about the wrongs they've done to me, I'll let myself be guided by my reason rather than by my anger.

original: The rarer action is   In virtue than in vengeance. They being penitent,   The sole drift of my purpose doth extend   Not a frown further.
translation: It's nobler to act honorably than to seek vengeance. Since they are sorry for what they did, there's nothing else that I want.

original: Go release them, Ariel.   My charms I’ll break, their senses I’ll restore,   And they shall be themselves.
translation: Go release them, Ariel. I’ll cut off my spells, return them to their normal senses, and they’ll be themselves again.

original: I’ll fetch them, sir.
translation: I’ll get them, sir.

original: [tracing a circle on the ground]   Ye elves of hills, brooks, standing lakes, and groves,   And ye that on the sands with printless foot   Do chase the ebbing Neptune and do fly him   When he comes back;
translation: [Drawing a large circle on the stage with his staff]  All you elves of hills, streams, lakes, and forests; and you elves who leave no footprints on the sand, chasing the ocean waves as they draw down the beach and running from those same waves when they come back;

original: you demi-puppets that   By moonshine do the green sour ringlets make,   Whereof the ewe not bites; and you whose pastime   Is to make midnight mushrooms,
translation: you puppet-sized creatures that by the light of the moon make fairy-rings in the grass, which a sheep will refuse to eat; and you who like to make mushrooms at midnight,

original: that rejoice   To hear the solemn curfew; by whose aid,   Weak masters though ye be, I have bedimmed   The noontide sun, called forth the mutinous winds,
translation: and who celebrate when you hear the bells signaling the arrival of night—with your help (though none of you are powerful) I've darkened the noon sun, summoned the rebellious winds,

original: And ’twixt the green sea and the azured vault   Set roaring war—to th' dread rattling thunder   Have I given fire, and rifted Jove’s stout oak   With his own bolt;
translation: and made the green sea and blue sky war against each other. I've shot off the dreadful rumbling thunderbolt, and burned up  Jupiter's  strong oak with his own lightning.

original: the strong-based promontory   Have I made shake, and by the spurs plucked up   The pine and cedar; graves at my command   Have waked their sleepers, oped, and let 'em forth   By my so potent art.
translation: I've made the sturdy cliffs shake, and pulled up pine and cedar trees by the roots. With my strong magic, I've woken the dead and opened their graves to let them out. But now I reject this wild magic.

original: But this rough magic   I here abjure, and when I have required   Some heavenly music, which even now I do,
translation: And after I have conjured some heavenly music—as I’m doing now—

original: To work mine end upon their senses that   This airy charm is for,   I’ll break my staff,
translation: to achieve my goal of affecting the senses of those at whom I aim my spell, I’ll break my staff.

original: Bury it certain fathoms in the earth,   And deeper than did ever plummet sound   I’ll drown my book.
translation: Then I'll bury it deep underground, and throw my book of magic into the sea so that it sinks farther than any anchor has ever reached.

original: A solemn air and the best comforter   To an unsettled fancy cure thy brains,   Now useless, boiled within thy skull. There stand,   For you are spell-stopped.
translation: Some solemn music is the best for comforting and curing restless minds, which right now are useless—burning with passions inside your skulls. All of you, stand there. You are under my spell.

original: Holy Gonzalo, honorable man,   Mine eyes, ev'n sociable to the show of thine,   Fall fellowly drops.
translation: [To GONZALO]  Good Gonzalo, you honorable man, I sympathize with what your crying eyes show that you are feeling, and my eyes cry too.

original: The charm dissolves apace,   And as the morning steals upon the night,   Melting the darkness, so their rising senses   Begin to chase the ignorant fumes that mantle   Their clearer reason.
translation: [To himself]  The spell is quickly dissipating, and like dawn sneaking up on the night and melting the darkness, their normal senses begin to creep up past the daze that right now clouds their minds.

original: O good Gonzalo,   My true preserver and a loyal sir   To him you follow’st, I will pay thy graces   Home both in word and deed.
translation: [To GONZALO]  Oh, good Gonzalo—my true savior and a loyal lord to the king you follow—I’ll reward everything you've done, both with words and actions.

original: Most cruelly   Didst thou, Alonso, use me and my daughter.   Thy brother was a furtherer in the act.
translation: [To ALONSO]  Alonso, you treated both my daughter and me cruelly, and your brother helped you do it.

original: Thou art pinched for ’t now, Sebastian.
translation: [To SEBASTIAN]  You’re being punished for it now, Sebastian.

original: Flesh and  blood,   You brother mine, that entertained ambition,   Expelled remorse and nature, whom, with Sebastian,   Whose inward pinches therefore are most strong,
translation: [To ANTONIO]  My brother, my flesh and blood, you followed your ambition and in so doing lost your goodness and compassion. It is because of you that Sebastian's guilty conscience is so strong,

original: Would here have killed your king—I do forgive thee,   Unnatural though thou art.
translation: because you would have killed your king with him. But I forgive you, even though you are a monster.

original: Their understanding   Begins to swell, and the approaching tide   Will shortly fill the reasonable shore   That now lies foul and muddy.
translation: [To himself]  Their minds are starting to return to normal, and soon their reason will emerge from where it is now muddied by confusion.

original: Not one of them   That yet looks on me, or would know me.
translation: Not one of them would recognize me yet.

original: Ariel,   Fetch me the hat and rapier in my cell.
translation: [To ARIEL]  Ariel, get me the hat and sword from my hut.

original: I will discase me, and myself present   As I was sometime Milan. Quickly, spirit.   Thou shalt ere long be free.
translation: I’ll take off the magician's robes I’m wearing, and put on the clothes I used to wear in Milan. Quickly, spirit. Not long from now, you will be free.

original: [sings and helps to attire PROSPERO]   Where the bee sucks, there suck I.   In a cowslip’s bell I lie.
translation: [Singing while helping PROSPERO dress] Where the bee drinks, I do too. In the cup of a cowslip flower is where I lie.

original: There I couch when owls do cry.   On the bat’s back I do fly   After summer merrily.
translation: That's where I sleep when the owls hoot. I fly on a bat’s back Joyfully chasing summer around the Earth.

original: Merrily, merrily shall I live now   Under the blossom that hangs on the bough.
translation: Happily, happily I will live now Under the blossom that hangs on the branch.

original: Why, that’s my dainty Ariel. I shall miss thee,   But yet thou shalt have freedom.—So, so, so.—   To the king’s ship, invisible as thou art.
translation: Why, that’s my dainty Ariel singing. I will miss you, but I will still give you your freedom. Yes, yes, yes. Go to the king’s ship, remaining invisible as you are right now.

original: There shalt thou find the mariners asleep   Under the hatches.
translation: There you’ll find the sailors asleep below deck.

original: The Master and the Boatswain   Being awake, enforce them to this place,   And presently, I prithee.
translation: The Master and Boatswain will be awake. Lead them here immediately, please.

original: I drink the air before me, and return Or ere your pulse twice beat.
translation: I’ll speed through the air in front of me, and I'll be back before your heart beats twice.

original: All torment, trouble, wonder, and amazement Inhabits here. Some heavenly power guide us Out of this fearful country!
translation: This is a place of suffering, trouble, awe, and amazement. May some heavenly power guide us out of this terrifying country!

original: [to ALONSO]   Behold, sir King,   The wrongèd Duke of Milan, Prospero.
translation: [To ALONSO]  Look, noble King, I am Prospero, the former Duke of Milan, who was wronged.

original: For more assurance that a living prince   Does now speak to thee, I embrace thy body.
translation: To prove to you that it's a real live person speaking to you, I will hug you.

original: And to thee and thy company I bid   A hearty welcome.   [embraces ALONSO]
translation: And I wish a warm welcome to you and to those with you.  [He hugs ALONSO]

original: Whe'er thou beest he or no,   Or some enchanted trifle to abuse me,   As late I have been, I not know.
translation: I don’t know whether or not you’re actually him, or if this is some magic trick designed to make me suffer, like I just was.

original: Thy pulse   Beats as of flesh and blood. And since I saw thee,   Th' affliction of my mind amends, with which   I fear a madness held me.
translation: Your heart beats like you are a flesh-and-blood man. And as soon as I saw you, the madness affecting my mind has eased.

original: This must crave—   An if this be at all—a most strange story.
translation: If it's actually true, then all of this requires an extraordinary explanation.

original: Thy dukedom I resign and do entreat   Thou pardon me my wrongs. But how should Prospero   Be living and be here?
translation: I hereby give up ownership of your dukedom, and beg you to forgive me for the wrongs I did to you. But how is it possible that Prospero is alive and on this island?

original: First, noble friend, Let me embrace thine age, whose honor cannot Be measured or confined.
translation: First, my noble old friend, let me hug you. Your honor is so great it can't be measured or contained.

original: Whether this be Or be not, I’ll not swear.
translation: I can't tell if any of this is real or not.

original: You do yet taste   Some subtleties o' th' isle, that will not let you   Believe things certain.
translation: You’re still affected by the magic and illusions of this island, which make it hard for you to believe that anything is real.

original: Welcome, my friends all.
translation: Welcome to all of you, my friends.

original: [aside to SEBASTIAN and ANTONIO]   But you, my brace of lords, were I so minded,   I here could pluck his highness' frown upon you   And justify you traitors.
translation: [To SEBASTIAN and ANTONIO so that only they can hear]  But if I wanted to, I could prove that the two of you were traitors. And then you'd face the King's anger.

original: At this time   I will tell no tales.
translation: But at the moment I won’t say anything.

original: The devil speaks in him.
translation: The devil is speaking through him.

original: No.—   [to ANTONIO]
translation: No.

original: For you, most wicked sir, whom to call brother   Would even infect my mouth, I do forgive   Thy rankest fault, all of them,
translation: [To ANTONIO]  For you, wicked sir, whom I couldn't call my brother without making myself sick, I forgive even your worst sin—and every sin as well.

original: a   nd require   My dukedom of thee, which perforce, I know,   Thou must restore.
translation: All I require is for you to return my dukedom to me—which, of course, I know you have to give me.

original: If thou beest Prospero,   Give us particulars of thy preservation,   How thou hast met us here,
translation: If you are Prospero, tell us the details of how you survived, and how you met us here

original: whom three hours since   Were wracked upon this shore, where I have lost—
translation: when just three hours ago we were shipwrecked and I lost my dear son Ferdinand.

original: How sharp the point of this remembrance is!   My dear son Ferdinand.
translation: How sharp the pain of this memory is!

original: I am woe for ’t, sir.
translation: I’m sorry about that, sir.

original: Irreparable is the loss, and patience Says it is past her cure.
translation: The loss can never be repaired, and patiently waiting for the pain to fade is not going to work.

original: I rather think   You have not sought her help,
translation: I think that you haven't actually tried patience,

original: of whose soft grace   For the like loss I have her sovereign aid,   And rest myself content.
translation: which has helped me get through a similar loss and find eventual happiness.

original: You the like loss?
translation: You've faced a loss like mine?

original: As great to me as late. And, supportable   To make the dear loss,
translation: Yes, as great and as recent. And, to make the loss more profound,

original: have I means much weaker   Than you may call to comfort you, for I   Have lost my daughter.
translation: I have much less to comfort me than you do, because I lost my daughter.

original: A daughter?   O heavens, that they were living both in Naples,   The king and queen there!
translation: A daughter? Oh God, I wish that they were both living in Naples, as king and queen of the country!

original: That they were, I wish   Myself were mudded in that oozy bed   Where my son lies.—When did you lose your daughter?
translation: To make that happen, I’d sacrifice my own life and lie in the muddy bed beneath the ocean. When did you lose your daughter?

original: In this last tempest. I perceive these lords   At this encounter do so much admire   That they devour their reason and scarce think   Their eyes do offices of truth, their words   Are natural breath.
translation: In the recent storm. It seems to me that these lords are so amazed to see me that they're standing there with their mouths open. They have lost use of their reason, don't believe their eyes, and can't speak.

original: But howsoev'r you have   Been justled from your senses, know for certain   That I am Prospero and that very duke   Which was thrust forth of Milan,
translation: Whatever has shocked you out of your senses, know for certain that I am Prospero. I am the duke who was thrown out of Milan

original: who most strangely   Upon this shore where you were wracked, was landed,   To be the lord on ’t.
translation: and landed on this same island where you were shipwrecked, and became the lord of it.

original: No more yet of this,   For ’tis a chronicle of day by day,   Not a relation for a breakfast, nor   Befitting this first meeting.
translation: That's enough of this story, because it's a tale that would take days to tell. It's not something you can describe over breakfast, and it's not appropriate to discuss during this first meeting.

original: [to ALONSO]   Welcome, sir.   This cell’s my court. Here have I few attendants   And subjects none abroad. Pray you, look in.
translation: [To ALONSO]   Welcome, sir. This hut is my royal court. I have just a few servants here, and none elsewhere on the island. Please, take a look around.

original: My dukedom since you have given me again,   I will requite you with as good a thing,   At least bring forth a wonder to content ye   As much as me my dukedom.
translation: Since you’ve returned my dukedom to me, I’ll give to you something just as nice in return. I’ll show you a wonder that will please you as much as my dukedom pleases me.

original: Sweet lord, you play me false.
translation: Sweet lord, you’re cheating.

original: No, my dearest love, I would not for the world.
translation: No, my dearest love, I would never do that, not for anything in the world.

original: Yes, for a score of kingdoms you should wrangle, And I would call it fair play.
translation: Well, you should do everything you can to win. Even if it was to gain just twenty kingdoms, I'd say you were right to do it.

original: If this prove A vision of the Island, one dear son Shall I twice lose.
translation: If this is just another of the illusions produced by this island, then I’ll lose my dear son twice.

original: A most high miracle!
translation: An incredible miracle!

original: Though the seas threaten, they are merciful. I have cursed them without cause.
translation: Though the seas threaten us sometimes, they are merciful because they let you survive. I was wrong to curse them.

original: Now all the blessings   Of a glad father, compass thee about.
translation: May all the blessings of a happy father surround you.

original: Arise, and say how thou camest here.
translation: Stand up, and tell me how you ended up here.

original: Oh, wonder!   How many goodly creatures are there here!
translation: Oh, it's wonderful! Look how many beautiful creatures there are here!

original: How beauteous mankind is! O brave new world,   That has such people in ’t!
translation: Mankind is so beautiful! Oh, splendid new world, that has such people in it!

original: 'Tis new to thee.
translation: It’s new to you.

original: [to FERDINAND]   What is this maid with whom thou wast at play?   Your eld’st acquaintance cannot be three hours.
translation: [To FERDINAND]  Who is this young woman with whom you were playing chess? You can’t have known her for more than three hours.

original: Is she the goddess that hath severed us   And brought us thus together?
translation: Is she the goddess that separated us and then brought us back together?

original: Sir, she is mortal.   But by immortal providence, she’s mine.   I chose her when I could not ask my father   For his advice, nor thought I had one.
translation: Sir, she’s human. But by God's blessing, she’s mine. I chose her to be my wife when I couldn't ask my father for his advice, and in fact no longer thought I had a father.

original: She   Is daughter to this famous Duke of Milan,   Of whom so often I have heard renown   But never saw before,
translation: She’s the daughter of this famous Duke of Milan, about whom I had heard such good things but had never seen before.

original: of whom I have   Received a second life. And second father   This lady makes him to me.
translation: I've been given a second life from him, and marrying her makes him a second father to me.

original: I am hers. But oh, how oddly will it sound that I Must ask my child forgiveness!
translation: And that makes me her father too. But oh, how strange it is that I have to ask my child to forgive me!

original: There, sir, stop. Let us not burden our remembrances with A heaviness that’s gone.
translation: Please, sir, no more of that. Let’s not weigh down our memories with a sadness that should be all in the past.

original: I have inly wept,   Or should have spoke ere this.
translation: I've just been crying to myself, or else I would have said something before now.

original: Look down, you gods,   And on this couple drop a blessèd crown,   For it is you that have chalked forth the way   Which brought us hither.
translation: Dear gods, look down from the sky and place a blessed crown on this couple, since it was you who led us on the path that brought us here.

original: I say, amen, Gonzalo.
translation: Yes, I say amen to that, Gonzalo.

original: Was Milan thrust from Milan, that his issue   Should become kings of Naples?
translation: Was the Duke of Milan thrown out of Milan so that his descendants could become kings of Naples?

original: O, rejoice   Beyond a common joy, and set it down   With gold on lasting pillars. In one voyage   Did Claribel her husband find at Tunis;
translation: Oh, we should celebrate this extraordinary joy, and commemorate it in gold letters, etching them into columns that will last forever. In just one journey, Claribel found a husband in Tunis;

original: And Ferdinand, her brother, found a wife   Where he himself was lost; Prospero, his dukedom   In a poor isle;
translation: Ferdinand, her brother, found a wife in the place where he was shipwrecked; Prospero found his dukedom on a deserted island;

original: and all of us, ourselves   When no man was his own.
translation: and all of us found ourselves when we could not control our own minds.

original: Give me your hands. Let grief and sorrow still embrace his heart That doth not wish you joy.
translation: Give me your hands. May grief and sorrow always grip the heart of anyone who does not wish you joy.

original: Be it so. Amen.
translation: So be it. Amen.

original: Oh, look, sir, look, sir! Here is more of us.   I prophesied if a gallows were on land,   This fellow could not drown.
translation: Oh, look, sir, look, sir! More of us are here. I predicted that so long as there were gallows where a man could be hanged on land, this man would never drown.

original: [To BOATSWAIN]   Now, blasphemy,   That swear’st grace o'erboard, not an oath on shore?   Hast thou no mouth by land? What is the news?
translation: [To BOATSWAIN]  Hey, you offensive man, who swore so much it was as if you threw God overboard—aren't you going to swear now that you're on land? What news do you have?

original: The best news is that we have safely found   Our king and company. The next, our ship—
translation: The best news is that we’ve found our king and his men alive and safe. The next best news is that our ship—

original: Which, but three glasses since, we gave out split—   Is tight and yare and bravely rigged as when   We first put out to sea.
translation: which we thought had split in half just three hours ago—is as well-constructed, seaworthy, and well-supplied as it was when we first set sail.

original: Sir, all this service Have I done since I went.
translation: Sir, all of what he describes is the work I’ve done since I left you.

original: My tricksy spirit!
translation: My ingenious spirit!

original: These are not natural events. They strengthen From strange to stranger.—     Say, how came you hither?
translation: These events are not natural. They keep getting stranger and stranger. Tell me, how did you get here?

original: If I did think, sir, I were well awake,   I’d strive to tell you.
translation: Sir, if I thought that I was actually awake, I’d try to tell you.

original: We were dead of sleep   And—how, we know not—all clapped under hatches,   Where but even now with strange and several noises   Of roaring, shrieking, howling, jingling chains,
translation: We were fast asleep and—we don’t know how—we were below decks, when we heard all these different, strange noises: roaring, shrieking, howling, jingling chains, and more.

original: And more diversity of sounds, all horrible,   We were awaked, straightway at liberty,   Where we, in all her trim, freshly beheld   Our royal, good, and gallant ship,
translation: All of these noises were so horrible that they woke us up. Immediately we were free, and we saw our courageous ship.

original: our Master   Capering to eye her. On a trice, so please you,   Even in a dream were we divided from them   And were brought moping hither.
translation: The master danced with joy when he saw it. An instant later, as if in a dream, we were separated from the others and brought here in a daze.

original: Was ’t well done?
translation: Was the job well done?

original: Bravely, my diligence. Thou shalt be  free.
translation: Magnificently done, my hard-working spirit. You’ll get your freedom.

original: This is as strange a maze as e'er men trod,   And there is in this business more than nature   Was ever conduct of.
translation: This is as strange an experience as men have ever had. And it’s clear that there's more to what happened than natural causes can explain.

original: Some oracle   Must rectify our knowledge.
translation: We need some priest or prophet to explain what happened.

original: Sir, my liege,   Do not infest your mind with beating on   The strangeness of this business.
translation: Sir, my king, don’t waste your time obsessing about the strangeness of what's happened.

original: At picked leisure   Which shall be shortly, single I’ll resolve you—   Which to you shall seem probable—of every   These happened accidents.
translation: At the right time, which will be soon, I myself will explain—and it will be an explanation that you'll think is reasonable—about everything that's occurred.

original: Till when, be cheerful   And think of each thing well.
translation: Until then, be cheerful and be generous in your thoughts about each thing that's happened.

original: [aside to ARIEL]   Come hither, spirit.   Set Caliban and his companions free.   Untie the spell.
translation: [To ARIEL so that only he can hear]  Come here, spirit. Set Caliban and his companions free. Undo the spell that binds them.

original: How   fares my gracious sir?
translation: How are you, my king?

original: There are yet missing of your company   Some few odd lads that you remember not.
translation: There are a few men who were on your ship that are still missing—a few odd boys that you don't remember.

original: Every man shift for all the rest and let no man take  care for himself, for all is but fortune. Coraggio,  bully-monster, coraggio!
translation: Every man help everyone else, and don’t look out only for yourself, because everything that happens is just a product of blind luck. Courage, you noble monster, courage!

original: If these be true spies which I wear in my head, here’s  a goodly sight.
translation: If I can trust my eyes, this is a beautiful sight.

original: O Setebos, these be brave spirits indeed!   How fine my master is!
translation: Oh,  Setebos , these are really beautiful spirits! How amazing my master is!

original: I am afraid   He will chastise me.
translation: I’m afraid he’ll punish me.

original: Ha, ha! What things are these, my lord Antonio? Will money buy 'em?
translation: Ha, ha! What are these things here that we're seeing, my lord Antonio? Can you buy them with money?

original: Very like. One of them Is a plain fish, and no doubt marketable.
translation: Certainly. One of them looks exactly like a fish, and must therefore be marketable.

original: Mark but the badges of these men, my lords,   Then say if they be true.
translation: Take a look at the  badges  they wear indicating for whom they work, then tell me if they are honest.

original: [indicates CALIBAN]     This misshapen knave,   His mother was a witch, and one so strong   That could control the moon, make flows and ebbs,   And deal in her command without her power.
translation: This ugly monster  [He points at CALIBAN]  had a mother who was a witch so powerful that she could control the moon and the tides.

original: These three have robbed me, and this demi-devil—   For he’s a bastard one—had plotted with them   To take my life.
translation: These three have stolen from me. And this half-devil—only half-devil because he's a bastard—plotted with them to kill me.

original: Two of these fellows you   Must know and own. This thing of darkness I   Acknowledge mine.
translation: You must recognize two of these men, and accept responsibility for them. I admit that this dark monster is mine.

original: I shall be pinched to death.
translation: He’ll torture me to death.

original: Is not this Stephano, my drunken butler?
translation: Isn’t this Stephano, my drunken butler?

original: He is drunk now. Where had he wine?
translation: He’s drunk right now. Where did he get wine?

original: And Trinculo is reeling ripe. Where should they   Find this grand liquor that hath gilded 'em?—
translation: And Trinculo is so drunk that he's staggering. Where did they find the powerful liquor that has made them so drunk?

original: How camest thou in this pickle?
translation: [To TRINCULO]  How did you get so drunk?

original: I have been in such a pickle since I saw you last that, I fear me, will never out of my bones. I shall not fear flyblowing.
translation: I’ve been so drunk since I last saw you that I fear I’ll never get the alcohol out of my bones. But at least I won't have to fear rotting, since the alcohol will keep me so well-preserved.

original: Why, how now, Stephano?
translation: Well, how are you, Stephano?

original: O, touch me not. I am not Stephano, but a cramp.
translation: Oh, don’t touch me. I’m not Stephano, I’m just a cramp on two legs.

original: You’d be king o' th' isle, sirrah?
I should have been a sore one then.
translation: I would’ve been a dreadful king, then.

original: This is a strange thing as e'er I looked on.
translation: This is the strangest thing I've ever seen.

original: He is as disproportioned in his manners   As in his shape.—
[to CALIBAN]   Go, sirrah, to my cell.   Take with you your companions.
translation: [To CALIBAN]  Go, sir, to my hut. Take your companions with you.

original: As you look   To have my pardon, trim it handsomely.
translation: If you hope for my forgiveness, clean it well.

original: Ay, that I will. And I’ll be wise hereafter   And seek for grace.
translation: Yes, I'll do that. And from now on I'll be smart and always try to be good.

original: What a thrice-double ass   Was I, to take this drunkard for a god   And worship this dull fool!
translation: What a magnificent jackass I was, to think this drunkard was a god and worship the dumb fool!

original: Go to, away.
translation: Get going, go.

original: Hence, and bestow your luggage where you found it.
translation: Go, and return that trash you're wearing to where you found it.

original: Or stole it, rather.
translation: Or stole it, rather.

original: Sir, I invite your highness and your train   To my poor cell, where you shall take your rest   For this one night,
translation: Sir, I invite your Highness and your men to my little hut, where you can sleep tonight.

original: which—part of it—I’ll waste   With such discourse as, I not doubt, shall make it   Go quick away: the story of my life   And the particular accidents gone by   Since I came to this isle.
translation: I'll spend part of the night telling you a tale that will make the time pass quickly—the story of my life, and everything that happened since I first arrived on this island.

original: And in the morn   I’ll bring you to your ship and so to Naples,   Where I have hope to see the nuptial   Of these our dear-belovèd solemnized,
translation: And in the morning I’ll bring you to your ship and we'll all go to Naples, where I hope to see the wedding of our two beloved children.

original: And thence retire me to my Milan, where   Every third thought shall be my grave.
translation: From there, with my work completed, I will retire to Milan, where I’ll spend my time contemplating my coming death.

original: I long To hear the story of your life, which must Take the ear strangely.
translation: I can't wait to hear the story of your life, which must be an extraordinary thing to hear.

original: I’ll deliver all,   And promise you calm seas, auspicious gales,   And sail so expeditious that shall catch   Your royal fleet far off.—
translation: I’ll tell everything, and I promise to give you calm seas, favorable winds, and a journey so fast that you’ll catch up with the now distant royal navy before you reach Milan.

original: [aside to ARIEL]   My Ariel,  chick,   That is thy charge. Then to the elements   Be free, and fare thou well!—
translation: [To ARIEL so that only he can hear]  My Ariel, little one, making all that I've just said happen is your responsibility. Once that is done, you are free to go where you wish, and farewell!

original: Please you, draw near.
translation: [To all the others]  Please, all of you, come close.

original: Now my charms are all o'erthrown,   And what strength I have’s mine own,   Which is most faint.
translation: Now my spells are all finished, and the strength that I have left is just my own—which is quite weak.

original: Now, ’tis true,   I must be here confined by you,   Or sent to Naples.
translation: Now, it's true, I'll either be kept in this place by you, the audience, or get to go to Naples.

original: Let me not,   Since I have my dukedom got   And pardoned the deceiver, dwell   In this bare island by your spell,
translation: Please, since I have gotten back my dukedom and forgiven the one who betrayed me, do not keep me here on this deserted island with your spells.

original: But release me from my bands   With the help of your good hands.
translation: Instead, use your hands to applaud, and free me from my constraints.

original: Gentle breath of yours my sails   Must fill, or else my project fails,   Which was to please.
translation: Your kind cheers will fill the sails of my ship, or else I will have failed to reach my goal, which was to please you.

original: Now I want   Spirits to enforce, art to enchant,
translation: Now I lack both spirits to command, and also the ability to do magic.

original: And my ending is despair,   Unless I be relieved by prayer,   Which pierces so that it assaults   Mercy itself and frees all faults.
translation: I'll end up in despair unless my request touches your compassion, and you forgive all the faults of this production.

original: As you from crimes would pardoned be,   Let your indulgence set me free.
translation: Just as you would be forgiven for your sins, be generous in your response to our play, and set me free.

original: If music be the food of love, play on.   Give me excess of it that, surfeiting,   The appetite may sicken, and so die.
translation: If music feeds love and makes it stronger, then keep playing music. Give me too much of it, so much that it kills my longing for love and makes it go away.

original: That strain again, it had a dying fall.   O, it came o'er my ear like the sweet sound,   That breathes upon a bank of violets,   Stealing and giving odor.
translation: Play that part again—it sounded melancholy. Oh, it sounded to me like a sweet breeze blowing over a bank of violets, stealing their scent and distributing it to everyone.

original: Enough, no more.   'Tis not so sweet now as it was before.
translation: That's enough now, no more music. It doesn't sound as sweet as it did before.

original: O spirit of love, how quick and fresh art thou,   That, notwithstanding thy capacity   Receiveth as the sea, nought enters there,   Of what validity and pitch soe'er,
translation: Oh spirit of love, how restless you are! You make me want to accept everything, like the sea does,

original: But falls into abatement and low price   Even in a minute.
translation: but then the next minute everything seems worthless, no matter how valuable it is.

original: So full of shapes is fancy   That it alone is high fantastical.
translation: Love is like a hallucination—nothing else is so imaginative and extravagant.

original: Will you go hunt, my lord?
translation: Do you want to go hunting, my lord?

original: What, Curio?
translation: Hunting what, Curio?

original: The hart.
translation: The hart.

original: Why, so I do, the noblest that I have.
translation: I am already hunting a  hart , but it's also  my  heart being hunted.

original: Oh, when mine eyes did see Olivia first,   Methought she purged the air of pestilence.
translation: Oh, when I first saw Olivia, it seemed to me that she purified the air with her very presence.

original: That instant was I turned into a hart,   And my desires, like fell and cruel hounds,   E'er since pursue me.
translation: In that instant I was transformed into a hart, and ever since then my desire for her has pursued me like a pack of cruel hunting hounds.

original: How now! What news from her?
translation: What's going on? What's the news from her?

original: So please my lord, I might not be admitted,   But from her handmaid do return this answer:
translation: I'm sorry, my lord, they wouldn't let me enter, but Olivia's handmaid gave me this answer:

original: The element itself, till seven years' heat,   Shall not behold her face at ample view,
translation: the outside world won't see Olivia's face for the next seven years.

original: But like a cloistress, she will veiled walk   And water once a day her chamber round   With eye-offending brine
translation: She'll wear a  veil  like a nun, and once a day she'll water her room with her tears.

original: —all this to season   A brother’s dead love, which she would keep fresh   And lasting in her sad remembrance.
translation: All of this is to preserve her love for her dead brother, whose memory she wants to keep fresh forever.

original: O, she that hath a heart of that fine frame   To pay this debt of love but to a brother,
translation: Oh, if the heart inside Olivia's beautiful body loves her brother this much,

original: How will she love, when the rich golden shaft   Hath killed the flock of all affections else   That live in her, when liver, brain, and heart,   These sovereign thrones, are all supplied, and filled   Her sweet perfections with one self king!
translation: then imagine how she will love  me  once Cupid's arrow has killed all her other emotions except love! Her mind, heart, and body—each of them a precious kingdom—will all be ruled by one man—me!

original: Away before me to sweet beds of flowers.   Love thoughts lie rich when canopied with bowers.
translation: Now take me to a garden of flowers. My thoughts of love will be strengthened by a beautiful setting.

original: What country, friends, is this?
translation: What country is this, friends?

original: This is Illyria, lady.
And what should I do in Illyria?   My brother he is in Elysium.
translation: And what should I do in Illyria? My brother is in  Heaven .

original: Perchance he is not drown’d.—What think you, sailors?
translation: Or perhaps there's a chance he didn't drown. What do you think, sailors?

original: It is perchance that you yourself were saved.
translation: It was only by chance that you yourself were saved.

original: O, my poor brother! And so perchance may he be.
