translation: [Giving the Sheriff a paper]  Angelo has sent you this note, and has also asked me to tell you not to overlook even the smallest part of it

original: neither in time, matter, or   other circumstance. Good morrow; for, as I take it,   it is almost day.
translation: when it comes to timing, what to do, or other circumstances. Good morning—since, as far as I can tell, it's almost day.

original: I shall obey him.
translation: I'll obey him.

original: [aside]   This is his pardon, purchased by such sin   For which the pardoner himself is in.
translation: [To himself]  This is his pardon, which was earned by committing a sin with the pardoner himself.

original: Hence hath offence his quick celerity,   When it is born in high authority:
translation: Look how quickly wrongdoing can work when it's done by someone with authority.

original: When vice makes mercy, mercy's so extended,   That for the fault's love is the offender friended.
translation: When sin leads to mercy, mercy extends itself to befriend the offender for the sake of his fault.

original: Now, sir, what news?
translation: [To PROVOST]  Now, sir, what's the news?

original: I told you. Lord Angelo, belike thinking me remiss in mine office, awakens me with this unwonted putting-on; methinks strangely, for he hath not used it before.
translation: I told you. Lord Angelo—who thinks I'm not very good at my job—has woken me up with all this. I think it's strange; he's never done it before.

original: Pray you, let's hear.
translation: Let's hear it, then.

original: [Reads]   'Whatsoever you may hear to the contrary, let   Claudio be executed by four of the clock; and in the   afternoon Barnardine:
translation: [Reading from the paper] "Whatever you might hear to the contrary, make sure Claudio is executed by four o'clock, and Barnadine in the afternoon.

original: for my better satisfaction,   let me have Claudio's head sent me by five.
translation: So that I can be sure, send me Claudio's head by five.

original: Let   this be duly performed; with a thought that more   depends on it than we must yet deliver.
translation: Do this exactly as I say, and keep in mind that more depends on it than just what we do.

original: Thus fail   not to do your office, as you will answer it at your  peril.'
translation: Don't fail to do what you're supposed to, or you'll answer for it at your own risk."

original: What say you to this, sir?
translation: [To DUKE VINCENTIO]  What do you say to that, sir?

original: What is that Barnardine who is to be executed in the afternoon?
translation: Who is this Barnadine that's supposed to be executed in the afternoon?

original: A Bohemian born, but here nursed un and bred; one that is a prisoner nine years old.
translation: He's Czech by birth, but he grew up here. He's been a prisoner for nine years.

original: How came it that the absent duke had not either delivered him to his liberty or executed him? I have heard it was ever his manner to do so.
translation: How come the absent Duke didn't either set him free or execute him? I've heard he typically used to do that.

original: His friends still wrought reprieves for him: and, indeed, his fact, till now in the government of Lord Angelo, came not to an undoubtful proof.
translation: His friends kept asking us to set him free. And, in fact, his case was unsettled until now, under Lord Angelo.

original: It is now apparent?
translation: Is it settled now?

original: Most manifest, and not denied by himself.
translation: Completely. Barnadine himself doesn't deny his crime.

original: Hath he born himself penitently in prison? how seems he to be touched?
translation: Has he seemed remorseful in prison? Does he regret it?

original: A man that apprehends death no more dreadfully but   as a drunken sleep;
translation: He's about as afraid of death as he is of a drunken sleep.

original: careless, reckless, and fearless   of what's past, present, or to come; insensible of   mortality, and desperately mortal.
translation: He's careless, reckless, and fearless of the past, present, and future. He doesn't care about his own mortality, even though he's a mortal man.

original: He wants advice.
translation: He needs advice.

original: He will hear none: he hath evermore had the liberty   of the prison;
translation: He won't listen to it. He likes being in prison.

original: give him leave to escape hence, he   would not: drunk many times a day, if not many days   entirely drunk.
translation: If you gave him the opportunity to escape, he wouldn't. He's drunk several times a day, and some days he's drunk all day.

original: We have very oft awaked him, as if   to carry him to execution, and showed him a seeming   warrant for it: it hath not moved him at all.
translation: We have often tried to wake him, as if we were about to execute him—even though we didn't have a warrant for it—and he didn't care at all.

original: More of him anon. There is written in your brow,   provost, honesty and constancy:
translation: I want to hear more about him later. Provost, I can tell that you're an honest, dependable man.

original: if I read it not   truly, my ancient skill beguiles me; but, in the   boldness of my cunning, I will lay myself in hazard.
translation: If I'm wrong, then my lifelong skills have failed me. But I'll trust my instinct and take the risk.

original: Claudio, whom here you have warrant to execute, is   no greater forfeit to the law than Angelo who hath   sentenced him.
translation: Although you have a warrant here for Claudio's execution, Claudio is no more guilty under the law than Angelo, the man who sentenced him.

original: To make you understand this in a   manifested effect, I crave but four days' respite;   for the which you are to do me both a present and a   dangerous courtesy.
translation: If you give me four days, I can prove this to you completely. In the meantime, I need you to do me an immediate and dangerous favor.

original: Pray, sir, in what?
translation: What's that, sir?

original: In the delaying death.
translation: I need you to delay the death.

original: A lack, how may I do it, having the hour limited,   and an express command, under penalty, to deliver   his head in the view of Angelo?
translation: But how can I do it? The hour's been set and I have an express command—under threat—to bring Claudio's head to Angelo!

original: I may make my case   as Claudio's, to cross this in the smallest.
translation: I'll be sentenced to die like Claudio if I mess this up in the slightest.

original: By the vow of mine order I warrant you, if my instructions may be your guide. Let this Barnardine be this morning executed, and his head born to Angelo.
translation: I swear by the vow I made to my order that you'll be safe if you can follow my instructions. Have Barnadine executed this morning, and send his head to Angelo.

original: Angelo hath seen them both, and will discover the  favour.
translation: Angelo has seen both of them—he'll figure out the swap.

original: O, death's a great disguiser; and you may add to it.
translation: Oh, death changes the way people look—and you can add to it.

original: Shave the head, and tie the beard; and say it was   the desire of the penitent to be so bared before his   death: you know the course is common.
translation: Shave the head and tie the beard. Say it was the dead man's desire to be shaved before death; you know it's a common thing.

original: If any thing   fall to you upon this, more than thanks and good   fortune, by the saint whom I profess, I will plead   against it with my life.
translation: If you get any trouble because of this, I swear by my patron saint that I will fight for you with my life.

original: Pardon me, good father; it is against my oath.
translation: Forgive me, good father. But it goes against my promise.

original: Were you sworn to the duke, or to the deputy?
translation: Did you swear to the Duke, or to the deputy?

original: To him, and to his substitutes.
translation: To the Duke and to his substitutes.

original: You will think you have made no offence, if the duke avouch the justice of your dealing?
translation: Will you believe you've done nothing wrong if the Duke signs off on what you're doing?

original: But what likelihood is in that?
translation: But what's the chance of that?

original: Not a resemblance, but a certainty. Yet since I see   you fearful,
translation: It's not only possible, it's certain. But since I can tell that you're afraid

original: that neither my coat, integrity, nor   persuasion can with ease attempt you,
translation: —and that my outfit, my integrity, and my argument can't convince you

original: I will go   further than I meant, to pluck all fears out of you.
translation: —I'll go further than I meant to go to put you at ease.

original: Look you, sir, here is the hand and seal of the   duke: you know the character, I doubt not; and the   signet is not strange to you.
translation: Look here, sir: this is the handwriting and seal of the Duke. You know his handwriting, I'm sure, and the seal is familiar to you?

original: I know them both.
translation: I know both of them.

original: The contents of this is the return of the duke: you   shall anon over-read it at your pleasure; where you   shall find, within these two days he will be here.
translation: Then consider this letter like the return of the Duke. Later, you can read over it as much as you like, and you'll find out that he'll be here in two days.

original: This is a thing that Angelo knows not; for he this   very day receives letters of strange tenor;
translation: Angelo doesn't know that. Today he's received some strange letters

original: perchance of the duke's death; perchance entering   into some monastery;
translation: —possibly about the Duke's death, or about him going into a monastery.

original: but, by chance, nothing of what   is writ. Look, the unfolding star calls up the   shepherd.
translation: But he doesn't know anything about what's written here. Look, you'll be guided just like the shepherds were guided to Jesus' manger by the  star  in Bethlehem.

original: Put not yourself into amazement how these   things should be: all difficulties are but easy   when they are known.
translation: You shouldn't be afraid of these things, since problems become much easier once we figure out what they are.

original: Call your executioner, and off   with Barnardine's head: I will give him a present   shrift and advise him for a better place.
translation: Call your executioner and tell him to chop off Barnadine's head. I'll give him his last confession and prepare him for what's after death.

original: Yet you   are amazed; but this shall absolutely resolve you.   Come away; it is almost clear dawn.
translation: You still seem amazed. But this letter will make up your mind. Come on, let's go; it's almost completely light out.

original: I am as well acquainted here as I was in our house   of profession:
translation: I feel just as much at home here as I felt at the brothel.

original: one would think it were Mistress   Overdone's own house, for here be many of her old   customers.
translation: You'd think it was Mistress Overdone's own place, considering so many of her customers are here.

original: First, here's young Master Rash; he's in   for a commodity of brown paper and old ginger,   ninescore and seventeen pounds;
translation: First, here's young Mr.  Rash . He's in for  lending  money through the stock commodities of brown paper and old ginger—one hundred ninety-seven pounds-

original: of which he made   five marks, ready money: marry, then ginger was not   much in request, for the old women were all dead.
translation: -and he made five pounds of ready money. But by then no one wanted the ginger, since his borrowers were all dead!

original: Then is there here one Master Caper, at the suit of   Master Three-pile the mercer, for some four suits of   peach-coloured satin, which now peaches him a   beggar.
translation: And here we have Mr. Caper who's here because of his debt to Mr. Three-Fold the cloth-maker for four peach-colored satin suits, which have caused him to go bankrupt.

original: Then have we here young Dizy, and young   Master Deep-vow, and Master Copperspur, and Master   Starve-lackey the rapier and dagger man, and young   Drop-heir that killed lusty Pudding,
translation: Then we have Dunce, and Mr. Swearsalot, and Mr. Fools-Gold, and Mr. Starving-Servant the swordsman, and young Mr. Son-Slayer who killed the vivacious Pudding,

original: and Master   Forthlight the tilter, and brave Master Shooty the   great traveller, and wild Half-can that stabbed   Pots,
translation: and Mr. Bullseye the jouster, and brave Mr. Shoe-Tie who travels a lot, and crazy Half-Pint who stabbed Pots,

original: and, I think, forty more; all great doers in   our trade, and are now "for the Lord's sake."
translation: and, I think, forty more—all the best customers in our business, all here "for the Lord's sake."

original: Sirrah, bring Barnardine hither.
translation: Sir, bring Barnadine here.

original: Master Barnardine! you must rise and be hanged. Master Barnardine!
translation: Mr. Barnadine! You have to get up and be hanged! Mr. Barnadine!

original: What, ho, Barnardine!
translation: Hello there, Barnadine!

original: A pox o' your throats! Who makes that noise there? What are you?
translation: A curse on both of you! Who's making noise out there? Who are you?

original: Your friends, sir; the hangman. You must be so good, sir, to rise and be put to death.
translation: Your friends, sir, the executioners. Sir, you need to do us the favor of getting up and being put to death.

original: Away, you rogue, away! I am sleepy.
translation: Go away, you rascal! I'm sleepy.

original: Tell him he must awake, and that quickly too.
translation: Tell him he has to wake up—and quickly too.

original: Pray, Master Barnardine, awake till you are executed, and sleep afterwards.
translation: Please, Mr. Barnadine, stay awake until you're executed; you can sleep afterward.

original: Go in to him, and fetch him out.
translation: Go get him and bring him out.

original: He is coming, sir, he is coming; I hear his straw  rustle.
translation: He's coming sir, he's coming. I can hear his straw rustling.

original: Is the axe upon the block, sirrah?
translation: Is the ax on the block, man?

original: Very ready, sir.
translation: It's ready, sir.

original: How now, Abhorson? what's the news with you?
translation: How are you, Abhorson? What's new with you?

original: Truly, sir, I would desire you to clap into your prayers; for, look you, the warrant's come.
translation: Really, sir, I need you to say your prayers. Look: the warrant is here.

original: You rogue, I have been drinking all night; I am not fitted for 't.
translation: You rascal, I've been drinking all night. I'm not ready for it.

original: O, the better, sir; for he that drinks all night, and is hanged betimes in the morning, may sleep the sounder all the next day.
translation: It's better that way, sir. If you drink all night and are executed in the morning, you sleep better the whole next day.

original: Look you, sir; here comes your ghostly father: do we jest now, think you?
translation: Look, sir. Here comes the friar, your confessor. Do you still think we're joking now?

original: Sir, induced by my charity, and hearing how hastily you are to depart, I am come to advise you, comfort you and pray with you.
translation: Sir, because I'm a charitable man and I heard you're meant to die soon, I came to talk with you, comfort you, and pray with you.

original: Friar, not I. I have been drinking hard all night,   and I will have more time to prepare me,
translation: Friar, I won't. I've been drinking hard all night and need more time to get ready.

original: or they   shall beat out my brains with billets: I will not   consent to die this day, that's certain.
translation: Otherwise they'll have to beat my brains out with clubs. I won't agree to die today, that's for sure.

original: O, sir, you must: and therefore I beseech you Look forward on the journey you shall go.
translation: Oh, sir, you have to. I'm asking you to think about where you're headed.

original: I swear I will not die to-day for any man's persuasion.
translation: I swear I won't die today, no matter what anyone says.

original: But hear you.
translation: But listen—

original: Not a word: if you have any thing to say to me, come to my ward; for thence will not I to-day.
translation: Don't say another word. If you have anything to say to me, come into my cell. I'm not leaving there today.

original: Unfit to live or die: O gravel heart! After him, fellows; bring him to the block.
translation: He's doesn't deserve to live, and he refuses to die. What a hard heart! Go after him, men, and bring him to be executed.

original: Now, sir, how do you find the prisoner?
translation: Now, sir, how's the prisoner doing?

original: A creature unprepared, unmeet for death; And to transport him in the mind he is Were damnable.
Here in the prison, father,   There died this morning of a cruel fever   One Ragozine, a most notorious pirate,
translation: Father, this morning in the prison a man named Ragozine—a notorious pirate—died of a terrible fever.

original: A man of Claudio's years; his beard and head   Just of his colour.
translation: He's about Claudio's age—his beard and complexion were about the same as his.

original: What if we do omit   This reprobate till he were well inclined;
translation: What if we let this delinquent go until he's up for it,

original: And satisfy the deputy with the visage   Of Ragozine, more like to Claudio?
translation: and send the deputy Ragazine's head—which is more like Claudio's anyway?

original: O   , 'tis an accident that heaven provides!   Dispatch it presently;
translation: Oh, God has worked this detail out for us! Do it immediately.

original: the hour draws on   Prefix'd by Angelo: see this be done,   And sent according to command;
translation: The time Angelo set is getting closer. Make sure this is done, and that the head is sent just as he commanded.

original: whiles I   Persuade this rude wretch willingly to die.
translation: Meanwhile, I'll try to convince this rude criminal to die willingly.

original: This shall be done, good father, presently.   But Barnardine must die this afternoon:
translation: It'll be done immediately, good father. But Barnadine has to die this afternoon.

original: And how shall we continue Claudio,   To save me from the danger that might come   If he were known alive?
translation: What should we do with Claudio, considering I could be in danger if anyone found out that he was still alive?

original: Let this be done.   Put them in secret holds, both Barnardine and Claudio:
translation: Do this: put both Barnadine and Claudio in secret cells.

original: Ere twice the sun hath made his journal greeting   To the under generation, you shall find   Your safety manifested.
translation: Before the sun has risen over the earth two times, you'll be completely safe.

original: I am your free dependant.
translation: I'm entirely at your service.

original: Quick, dispatch, and send the head to Angelo.
translation: Go quickly, and send Ragozine's head to Angelo.

original: Now will I write letters to Angelo,—   The provost, he shall bear them, whose contents   Shall witness to him I am near at home,
translation: Now I'll write a letter to Angelo, which the provost can bring him. I'll write to tell him that I'm close to home, and

original: And that, by great injunctions, I am bound   To enter publicly:
translation: —because of the circumstances—I have to make a public entrance.

original: him I'll desire   To meet me at the consecrated fount   A league below the city;
translation: I'll ask him to meet me at the holy spring a mile away from the city.

original: and from thence,   By cold gradation and well-balanced form,   We shall proceed with Angelo.
translation: From there I'll proceed coolly and carefully with Angelo.

original: Here is the head; I'll carry it myself.
translation: Here's the head. I'll carry it myself.

original: Convenient is it. Make a swift return; For I would commune with you of such things That want no ear but yours.
translation: That's convenient. Come back soon, since I want to talk with you about things I can't tell anyone else.

original: I'll make all speed.
translation: I'll go as quickly as possible.

original: Peace, ho, be here!
translation: Hello! Peace be with you!

original: The tongue of Isabel. She's come to know   If yet her brother's pardon be come hither:
translation: That's Isabella's voice. She wants to know if her brother's pardon has gotten here.

original: But I will keep her ignorant of her good,   To make her heavenly comforts of despair,   When it is least expected.
translation: I won't tell her the good news yet. I'll wait and tell her once she gets upset and she least expects it.

original: Ho, by your leave!
translation: Hello, may I come in?

original: Good morning to you, fair and gracious daughter.
translation: Good morning to you, my beautiful, gracious daughter.

original: The better, given me by so holy a man. Hath yet the deputy sent my brother's pardon?
translation: That's a high compliment coming from such a holy man. Has the deputy sent my brother's pardon yet?

original: He hath released him, Isabel, from the world: His head is off and sent to Angelo.
translation: He released him from the world, Isabella. They cut off his head and sent it to Angelo.

original: Nay, but it is not so.
translation: No, say it isn't so!

original: It is no other: show your wisdom, daughter, In your close patience.
translation: It's true. Show your wisdom by being patient, daughter.

original: O, I will to him and pluck out his eyes!
translation: Oh, I'll go to Angelo and scratch his eyes out!

original: You shall not be admitted to his sight.
translation: You won't be allowed to get near him.

original: Unhappy Claudio! wretched Isabel! Injurious world! most damned Angelo!
translation: Poor Claudio! Miserable Isabella! Unjust world! Most damned Angelo!

original: This nor hurts him nor profits you a jot;   Forbear it therefore; give your cause to heaven.
translation: This isn't hurting him, and it's not helping you. So stop it, and pray instead.

original: Mark what I say, which you shall find   By every syllable a faithful verity:
translation: Listen to what I say, since every word of it is true, as you'll come to realize.

original: The duke comes home to-morrow; nay, dry your eyes;
translation: The Duke is coming home tomorrow. Come on, dry your eyes.

original: One of our convent, and his confessor,   Gives me this instance: already he hath carried   Notice to Escalus and Angelo,   Who do prepare to meet him at the gates,
translation: Someone from my monastery—who's his confessor—told me that the Duke already sent letters to Escalus and Angelo asking them to meet him at the gates,

original: There to give up their power. If you can, pace your  wisdom   In that good path that I would wish it go,
translation: where they'll give up their power. If you can, follow the plan I've been laying out here.

original: And you shall have your bosom on this wretch,   Grace of the duke, revenges to your heart,   And general honour.
translation: If you do, you'll be able to reveal what Angelo did to you. The Duke will look kindly on you, and you'll have your revenge and general acclaim.

original: I am directed by you.
translation: I'll do what you say.

original: This letter, then, to Friar Peter give;   'Tis that he sent me of the duke's return:
translation: Then give this letter to Friar Peter; it's the one he sent me telling me about the Duke's return.

original: Say, by this token, I desire his company   At Mariana's house to-night.   Her cause and yours   I'll perfect him withal, and he shall bring you   Before the duke,
translation: Tell him in the reply that I want to see him at Mariana's house tonight. I'll tell him what's gone on with her and with you, and he'll bring you to the Duke.

original: and to the head of Angelo   Accuse him home and home. For my poor self,   I am combined by a sacred vow   And shall be absent.
translation: Then you can get right to the point and accuse Angelo. As for me, I have a holy obligation and won't be able to be there.

original: Wend you with this letter:   Command these fretting waters from your eyes   With a light heart; trust not my holy order,   If I pervert your course. Who's here?
translation: Make your way with this letter. Stop your crying, and be happy. If I'm leading you astray, then don't trust the Church! Who's there?

original: Good even. Friar, where's the provost?
translation: Good evening. Friar, where's the provost?

original: Not within, sir.
translation: He's not here, sir.

original: O pretty Isabella, I am pale at mine heart to see   thine eyes so red: thou must be patient.
translation: Oh, pretty Isabella, my heart hurts to see your eyes so red. You need to be patient.

original: I am fain   to dine and sup with water and bran; I dare not for   my head fill my belly; one fruitful meal would set   me to 't.
translation: I want to sit and have a hearty dinner with water and bread, but I don't want to eat  anything  that might get me going.

original: But they say the duke will be here   to-morrow. By my troth, Isabel, I loved thy brother:
translation: But they say the Duke will be here tomorrow. I swear that I loved your brother, Isabella.

original: if the old fantastical duke of dark corners had been   at home, he had lived.
translation: If our old, imaginative, womanizing Duke had been here, he would have lived.

original: Sir, the duke is marvellous little beholding to your reports; but the best is, he lives not in them.
translation: Sir, the Duke will have to thank you for those kind words. But, at the same time, they don't really describe him.

original: Friar, thou knowest not the duke so well as I do: he's a better woodman than thou takest him for.
translation: Friar, you don't know the Duke as well as I do. He's more of a ladies' man than you think he is.

original: Well, you'll answer this one day. Fare ye well.
translation: Well, you'll have to answer for that one day. Take care.

original: Nay, tarry; I'll go along with thee I can tell thee pretty tales of the duke.
translation: No, wait. I'll go with you so I can tell you funny stories about the Duke.

original: You have told me too many of him already, sir, if they be true; if not true, none were enough.
translation: You've told me too many about him already, if they're true, sir. If they're not true, I'd rather hear none at all.

original: I was once before him for getting a wench with child.
translation: Once he put me on trial for getting a girl pregnant.

original: Did you such a thing?
translation: Did you do such a thing?

original: Yes, marry, did I but I was fain to forswear it; they would else have married me to the rotten medlar.
translation: Well, yes, I did. But I was eager to deny it. Otherwise, they would have made me marry the slut.

original: Sir, your company is fairer than honest. Rest you well.
translation: Sir, you're better company in looks than you are when you talk. Take care.

original: By my troth, I'll go with thee to the lane's end: if bawdy talk offend you, we'll have very little of it. Nay, friar, I am a kind of burr; I shall stick.
translation: I think I'll go with you to the end of the road. If my raunchy talk offends you, I'll cut it out. No, friar, I'm like a burr—I'll stick to you.

original: Every letter he hath writ hath disvouched other.

This gentleman told somewhat of my tale,—

translation: But the next morning, after he got what he wanted, Angelo sent a warrant for my brother's death.

translation: I swear, you foolish scoundrel, you either don't know what you're saying, or you're out to get the deputy because you hate him.

translation: First of all, his reputation is perfect. Second, there's no reason he would so aggressively punish faults that he himself had.

translation: If he had done what you said, he would have compared your brother to himself, and not killed him after all.

translation: Someone put you up to this. Tell the truth, and tell us who told you to come here and complain.

translation: Is this all I get? Then oh, God above, help me to be patient

translation: and wait for the moment when you'll expose the evil that's here in this man!

translation: God bless you, sir, and may he keep you from unhappiness. I, so wronged, will leave without being believed!

translation: I knew you'd leave. Officer? Take her to prison!

translation: How can I allow such a loud-mouthed, scandalous voice to embarrass someone I care so much about?

translation: This is some kind of plot. Who knew about your plan to come here?

translation: A holy father, probably. Does anyone know this Lodowick?

translation: If he weren't a holy person, sir, I would have smacked him in the face for some of the things he said about you while you were gone.

translation: Bad things about me? This friar doesn't sound like a very good man. And he sent this horrible woman here to embarrass my deputy! Find this friar.

translation: Sir,  I saw her and the friar at the prison last night. A rude friar, an absolutely worthless man.

translation: Bless you, your royal Grace! I've stood by and heard people telling you lies.

translation: First of all, this woman has wrongfully accused the deputy.

translation: He's as devoid of wrongdoing as she is devoid of  Jesus .

translation: I thought so. Do you know this Friar Lodowick that she mentioned?

translation: And I promise that he didn't say anything against you, your Grace, as this man has reported.

translation: Sir, he did, and horribly. Believe it.

translation: Well, maybe he'll come to clear his name at some point, but he's sick at the moment; he has some strange fever.

translation: I came here on his behalf after he found out there was a complaint coming against Lord Angelo.

translation: He asked me to relay what he knew to be true, and what he knew to be false; he'll clear everything up as soon as you can get hold of him.

translation: First, for this woman Mariana. With her own confession,

translation: Mariana can disprove the testimonies on behalf of Angelo, who's so personally and vulgarly accused.

translation: Good friar, let's hear it.

translation: Can't you smile about this, Lord Angelo? For heaven's sake, foolish people are so conceited!

translation: Bring us some seats. Come on, Angelo, I'll sit this one out; you can be your own judge.

translation: [Pointing to MARIANA]  Is this the  witness , friar? First, make her show her face, and then have her speak.

translation: I'm sorry, sir, but I won't show my face until my husband tells me to.

translation: Oh, so you're married?

translation: No, my lord.

translation: Are you a virgin?

translation: No, my lord.

translation: Are you a widow, then?

translation: Not that either, my lord.

translation: Well, then you're nothing at all! You're not a virgin, a widow, or a wife?

translation: My lord, maybe she's a prostitute. Lots of them are not virgins, widows, or wives.

translation: Make that man quiet. I wish he'd be content to chatter to himself.

translation: Very well, my lord.

translation: I've slept with my husband, but my husband doesn't know that he ever  slept  with me.

translation: He was drunk then, my lord. That must've been it.

translation: If it would keep you quiet, I wish you were drunk, too!

translation: Very well, my lord.

translation: This doesn't have anything to do with Lord Angelo.

translation: I'm getting to that, my lord. The woman who accused him of assaulting her accuses my husband in the same way.

translation: My lord, she makes her charges against him based on the time when I held him in my arms and made love to him, as I'll explain.

translation: Is she charging someone besides me?

translation: Not that I know of.

translation: No? But you said "your husband."

translation: Well, exactly, my lord. Angelo is my husband. He thinks he knows he's never had sex with me. But he knows that he thinks he's had sex with Isabella.

translation: This is a strange accusation. Let us see your face.

translation: Since my husband's telling me to do so, I'll take off my veil now.

translation: [She removes her veil]  This is the face, you cruel man, which you used to say was worth looking at.

translation: This is the hand which you held when you promised to marry me. And this is the body which you thought was Isabella's,

translation: and which you had your way with in your garden shack, imagining it was her.

translation: Do you know this woman?

translation: Sir, that's enough!

translation: Enough, my lord.

translation: My lord, I have to admit I know this woman.

translation: Five years ago there was some talk about marriage between us, but it was broken off—partially because the dowry which was promised didn't materialize,

translation: and mainly because her reputation took a major hit.

translation: In the five years since then I haven't spoken to her, seen her, or heard from her—I swear.

translation: Noble prince, as much as light comes from the sky and words come from our breath;

translation: as much as truth makes sense and virtue is always truthful, I'm this man's betrothed wife —if we put any stock in words and vows.

translation: And, my good lord, last Tuesday night in his garden shack, he slept with me as his wife.

translation: If this isn't true, may I never get up from here, and be frozen forever as a marble statue!

translation: I smiled up until now, Now, my good lord, let me do justice. My patience is running out.

translation: I can see that these poor, tattle-tale women are just the tools of some more powerful person who's made them do this.

translation: My lord, allow me to figure out what's going on.

translation: Of course, gladly. Punish them as you see fit.

translation: [To FRIAR PETER and MARIANA]  You foolish friar, and you lying woman—you're in cahoots with the other woman who was taken away!

translation: , just because you swore by all the saints in heaven?

original: Were testimonies against his worth and credit   That's seal'd in approbation?
translation: Did you really think that you could support a testimony against someone as perfectly unshakably worthy and believable as Angelo

original: You, Lord Escalus,   Sit with my cousin; lend him your kind pains   To find out this abuse, whence 'tis derived.
translation: [To ESCALUS]  You, Lord Escalus: sit with Angelo. Help him figure out who's behind all this, and where it came from.

original: There is another friar that set them on;   Let him be sent for.
translation: There's another friar that put them up to this; bring him here.

original: Would he were here, my lord! for he indeed   Hath set the women on to this complaint:
translation: I wish he were here, sir! He did put these women up to making the complaint.

original: Your provost knows the place where he abides   And he may fetch him.
translation: Your provost knows where he lives and can get him.

original: Go do it instantly.
translation: Go do it, immediately.

original: And you, my noble and well-warranted cousin,   Whom it concerns to hear this matter forth,   Do with your injuries as seems you best,   In any chastisement:
translation: And you, my noble, completely justified cousin: it's your job to hear this case and dole out whatever punishments you see fit.

original: I for a while will leave you;   But stir not you till you have well determined   Upon these slanderers.
translation: I'll leave you here for a while, but don't move until you've completely ruled on these slanderers.

original: My lord, we'll do it throughly.
translation: Sir, we'll do it thoroughly.

original: Signior Lucio, did not you say you knew that Friar Lodowick to be a dishonest person?
translation: Mr. Lucio, didn't you say that, as far as you knew, Friar Lodowick was a dishonest person?

original: "Cucullus non facit monachum:" honest in nothing but in his clothes; and one that hath spoke most villanous speeches of the duke.
translation: "A holy habit doesn't make a friar devout." The most honest thing about him are his clothes. He's the one who said such awful things about the Duke.

original: We shall entreat you to abide here till he come and enforce them against him: we shall find this friar a notable fellow.
translation: We'll have to ask you to stay here until he comes, so you can accuse him of it. I'm sure we'll find that this friar is unique.

original: As any in Vienna, on my word.
translation: As much as any friar in Vienna, I swear.

original: Call that same Isabel here once again; I would speak  with her. @ @
translation: Bring Isabella here again; I want to speak with her.

original: Pray you, my lord, give me leave to question; you shall see how I'll handle her.
translation: Please, my lord, let me question her. You'll see how I handle her.

original: Not better than he, by her own report.
translation: No better than he did, according to what she said.

original: Say you?
translation: Do you think?

original: Marry, sir, I think, if you handled her privately, she would sooner confess: perchance, publicly, she'll be ashamed.
translation: Indeed, I do, sir. I think that if you talked to her privately she'd confess sooner. Publicly, she might be too ashamed.

original: I will go darkly to work with her.
That's the way; for women are light at midnight.
translation: That's the spirit. Women are best that way.

original: Come on, mistress: here's a gentlewoman denies all that you have said.
translation: Come on, miss. Here's a gentlewoman that denies everything you said.

original: My lord, here comes the rascal I spoke of; here with the provost.
translation: My lord, here comes the rascal I was talking about. He's here with the provost.

original: In very good time: speak not you to him till we call upon you.
translation: Perfect timing. Don't say anything until we tell you to.

original: Mum.
translation: Mum's the word.

original: Come, sir: did you set these women on to slander Lord Angelo? they have confessed you did.
translation: All right, sir. Did you ask these women to slander Lord Angelo? They confessed that you did.

original: 'Tis false.
translation: That's false.

original: How! know you where you are?
translation: What? Do you know where you are?

original: Respect to your great place! and let the devil Be sometime honour'd for his burning throne! Where is the duke? 'tis he should hear me speak.
translation: I respect you and your position as much as I respect the devil on his burning throne! Where's the Duke? He's the one who should hear my testimony.

original: The duke's in us; and we will hear you speak: Look you speak justly.
translation: We're the Duke's substitutes, and we'll listen to your testimony. Make sure you tell the truth.

original: Boldly, at least. But, O, poor souls,   Come you to seek the lamb here of the fox?
translation: I'll speak boldly, at least. But you poor souls have let the  fox  set you on a lamb.

original: Good night to your redress! Is the duke gone?   Then is your cause gone too.
translation: Is this how you solve things? Is the Duke gone? Then you have no power.

original: The duke's unjust,   Thus to retort your manifest appeal,   And put your trial in the villain's mouth   Which here you come to accuse.
translation: [To MARIANA]  The Duke is unjust to reverse your appeal and make you go on trial in front of the villain you came to accuse.

original: This is the rascal; this is he I spoke of.
translation: This is the rascal, this is the man I was talking about!

original: Why, thou unreverend and unhallow'd friar,   Is't not enough thou hast suborn'd these women   To accuse this worthy man,
translation: You blasphemous, unholy friar! Isn't it enough that you forced these women to accuse a good man?

original: but, in foul mouth   And in the witness of his proper ear,   To call him villain?
translation: Do you have to insult the man to his face, and call him a "villain?"

original: and then to glance from him   To the duke himself, to tax him with injustice?
translation: And then go on to call the Duke himself unjust?

original: Take him hence; to the rack with him! We'll touse you   Joint by joint, but we will know his purpose.   What "unjust!"
translation: Take him away, torture him! We'll twist you up joint by joint until we get the truth out of you. He said "unjust!"

original: Be not so hot; the duke   Dare no more stretch this finger of mine than he   Dare rack his own:
translation: Don't get so angry. The Duke wouldn't dare to touch my little finger as much as he would dare to hurt himself.

original: his subject am I not,   Nor here provincial.
translation: I'm not his subject; I'm not from here.

original: My business in this state   Made me a looker on here in Vienna,   Where I have seen corruption boil and bubble   Till it o'er-run the stew;
translation: Because I've had business here, I've been an onlooker in Vienna, where I've seen corruption boil and bubble until it ran over the sides of the pot.

original: laws for all faults,   But faults so countenanced, that the strong statutes   Stand like the forfeits in a barber's shop,   As much in mock as mark.
translation: There are laws against every crime, but the crimes are dealt with in such a way that the strong laws are a laughingstock, like bald men in a barber shop. They're not taken seriously at all.

original: Slander to the state! Away with him to prison!
translation: He's slandering the state! Take him away to prison!

original: What can you vouch against him, Signior Lucio? Is this the man that you did tell us of?
translation: What can you say against him, Mr. Lucio? Is this the man you told us about?

original: 'Tis he, my lord. Come hither, goodman baldpate: do you know me?
translation: Yes, it's him, sir. Come on, Mr. Baldie. Do you know who I am?

original: I remember you, sir, by the sound of your voice: I met you at the prison, in the absence of the duke.
translation: I remember you by the sound of your voice, sir. I met you at the prison while the Duke was gone.

original: O, did you so? And do you remember what you said of the duke?
translation: Oh, did you? And do you remember what you said about the Duke?

original: Most notedly, sir.
translation: Very well, sir.

original: Do you so, sir? And was the duke a fleshmonger, a fool, and a coward, as you then reported him to be?
translation: Do you, sir? And didn't you say the Duke was a womanizer, an idiot, and a coward?

original: You must, sir, change persons with me, ere you make that my report: you, indeed, spoke so of him; and much more, much worse.
translation: Sir, I think you'll have to switch places with me before you say that. It was you that said that about him—and much more, much worse.

original: O thou damnable fellow! Did not I pluck thee by the nose for thy speeches?
translation: Oh, you accursed man! Didn't I punch you in the face for what you said?

original: I protest I love the duke as I love myself.
translation: I have to say, I love the Duke as much as I love myself.

original: Hark, how the villain would close now, after his treasonable abuses!
translation: Listen how the scoundrel tries to cover it up now, after committing treason!

original: Such a fellow is not to be talked withal. Away with   him to prison!
translation: You can't reason with a man like that. Take him away to prison!

original: Where is the provost? Away with him   to prison! lay bolts enough upon him: let him   speak no more.
translation: Where is the provost? Take him away to prison! Lock him up and never let him speak again.

original: Away with those giglots too, and   with the other confederate companion!
translation: Take those whores, too, with their co-conspirator!

original: Stay, sir; stay awhile.
translation: Wait, sir. Wait a minute.

original: What, resists he? Help him, Lucio.
translation: What, is he resisting? Help him, Lucio.

original: Come, sir; come, sir; come, sir; foh, sir! Why, you   bald-pated, lying rascal, you must be hooded, must   you?
translation: Come on, sir; come on, sir; come on, sir. Hey, sir! What, you bald-headed, lying rascal, you have to keep your hood on, huh?

original: Show your knave's visage, with a pox to you!   show your sheep-biting face, and be hanged an hour!   Will't not off?   [Pulls off the friar's hood, and  discovers DUKE VINCENTIO]
translation: Show your foolish face, and damn you! Show your dirty, lying face, and go die! Take it off!  [LUCIO pulls off the friar's hood, revealing DUKE VINCENTIO to everyone]

original: Thou art the first knave that e'er madest a duke.
translation: You're the first idiot that ever made someone a duke.

original: First, provost, let me bail these gentle three.
translation: [To the PROVOST, gesturing toward ISABELLA, MARIANA, and CLAUDIO]  First, sheriff, let me bail out these three innocent people.

original: [to Lucio]   Sneak not away, sir; for the friar and you   Must have a word anon. Lay hold on him.
translation: [To LUCIO]  Don't sneak away, sir. The friar and you have more to say to each other. Grab him.

original: This may prove worse than hanging.
translation: This might end up worse than hanging.

original: [To ESCALUS]   What you have spoke I pardon: sit you  down:   We'll borrow place of him.
translation: [To ESCALUS]  I forgive you for what you said. Sit down; I'll take his place.

original: [To ANGELO]   Sir, by your leave.   Hast thou or word, or wit, or impudence,   That yet can do thee office?
translation: [To ANGELO]  Sir, with your permission: do you have anything to say for yourself—any witty reply that can improve your situation?

original: If thou hast,   Rely upon it till my tale be heard,   And hold no longer out.
translation: If you do, tell me now before I tell my story. Don't hold out any longer.

original: O my dread lord,   I should be guiltier than my guiltiness,   To think I can be undiscernible,
translation: Oh, my sovereign lord, I feel guiltier than guiltiness itself now that I know I didn't go undetected;

original: When I perceive your grace, like power divine,   Hath look'd upon my passes.
translation: now that I know that you—like God himself—saw everything I did, your Grace.

original: Then, good prince,   No longer session hold upon my shame,
translation: So, good prince, don't make me stand up here any longer in my shame.

original: But let my trial be mine own confession:   Immediate sentence then and sequent death   Is all the grace I beg.
translation: I'll cut my trial short with a confession. All I ask is an immediate sentence and, after that, death.

original: Come hither, Mariana. Say, wast thou e'er contracted to this woman?
translation: Come here, Mariana.  Tell me, were you ever engaged to this woman?

original: I was, my lord.
translation: I was, my lord.

original: Go take her hence, and marry her instantly.
translation: Go take her away, and marry her immediately.

original: Do you the office, friar; which consummate,
translation: [To FRIAR PETER]  Friar, you can do the service; once it's done, bring him back here.

original: Return him here again. Go with him, provost.
translation: [To the PROVOST]  You go with him, Provost.

original: My lord, I am more amazed at his dishonour Than at the strangeness of it.
translation: My lord, I'm more surprised by his dishonor than I am by the unexpected nature of it.

original: Come hither, Isabel.   Your friar is now your prince: as I was then   Advertising and holy to your business,
translation: Come here, Isabella. Your friar is really your ruler. Back when I was in my disguise, I gave you holy advice for your project.

original: Not changing heart with habit, I am still   Attorney'd at your service.
translation: I haven't changed who I am when I changed my clothes; I'm still completely at your service.

original: O, give me pardon, That I, your vassal, have employ'd and pain'd Your unknown sovereignty!
translation: Oh, forgive me, sir! I'm just your subject, and I ordered you around, not realizing you were the Duke!

original: You are pardon'd, Isabel:   And now, dear maid, be you as free to us.
translation: I forgive you, Isabella. And now, dear girl, forgive me, too.

original: Your brother's death, I know, sits at your heart;
translation: I know you're grieving for your brother's death.

original: And you may marvel why I obscured myself,   Labouring to save his life, and would not rather   Make rash remonstrance of my hidden power   Than let him so be lost.
translation: And I know that you're wondering why I stayed disguised the whole time I was trying to save his life, instead of using my hidden power to save him.

original: O most kind maid,   It was the swift celerity of his death,   Which I did think with slower foot came on,   That brain'd my purpose.
translation: Oh, sweet girl, his death came so quickly, and I thought we had more time. So I didn't do what I meant to.

original: But, peace be with him!   That life is better life, past fearing death,   Than that which lives to fear: make it your comfort,   So happy is your brother.
translation: God rest his soul! He's in a better place now, and doesn't have to be afraid of death anymore, the way he was in life. Take comfort in the fact that your brother is happy now.

original: I do, my lord.
translation: I do, my lord.

original: For this new-married man approaching here,   Whose salt imagination yet hath wrong'd   Your well defended honour, you must pardon   For Mariana's sake:
translation: As for this newly-married man who's now approaching—whose dirty mind has done you wrong—you need to forgive him for Mariana's sake.

original: but as he adjudged your brother,—   Being criminal, in double violation   Of sacred chastity and of promise-breach   Thereon dependent, for your brother's life,—
translation: But since he judged you brother—criminally committing a double violation of the laws of abstinence and honesty with which he charged Claudio-

original: The very mercy of the law cries out   Most audible, even from his proper tongue,   'An Angelo for Claudio, death for death!'
translation: -the law itself seems to dictate that Angelo should die for Claudio, death for death.

original: Haste still pays haste, and leisure answers leisure;   Like doth quit like, and MEASURE still FOR MEASURE.
translation: Fast for fast, slow for slow, like for like, and measure, too, for measure.

original: Then, Angelo, thy fault's thus manifested;   Which, though thou wouldst deny, denies thee vantage.
translation: So, Angelo, we all know your crime. Even if you would deny it, you can't escape.

original: We do condemn thee to the very block   Where Claudio stoop'd to death, and with like haste.   Away with him!
translation: I condemn you to the same block where Claudio was killed, and just as quickly. Take him away!

original: O my most gracious lord, I hope you will not mock me with a husband.
translation: Oh, my most gracious lord, I hope you won't tease me with a husband!

original: It is your husband mock'd you with a husband.   Consenting to the safeguard of your honour,   I thought your marriage fit;
translation: Your husband's the one that teased you with a husband. I though it was best for your reputation to have you married;

original: else imputation,   For that he knew you, might reproach your life   And choke your good to come;
translation: otherwise, you might have a difficult time in the future, since you had sex with him.

original: for his possessions,   Although by confiscation they are ours,   We do instate and widow you withal,   To buy you a better husband.
translation: As for his possessions, although I could confiscate them, you're now his widow—so you can have it all. Buy yourself a better husband.

original: O my dear lord, I crave no other, nor no better man.
translation: Oh, my dear lord, I don't want anyone else. I don't want a better man.

original: Never crave him; we are definitive.
translation: Stop wanting him. My word is final.

original: Gentle my liege,—
translation: But, sir—

original: You do but lose your labour. Away with him to death! @     Now, sir, to you.
translation: You're wasting your time. Take him away to death! Now, sir, to you.

original: O my good lord! Sweet Isabel, take my part;
translation: Oh, my good lord! Sweet Isabella, help me!

original: Lend me your knees, and all my life to come   I'll lend you all my life to do you service.
translation: Beg with me on your knees, and I'll owe you anything and everything for the rest of my life.

original: Against all sense you do importune her:
translation: It makes no sense for you to ask her.

original: Should she kneel down in mercy of this fact,   Her brother's ghost his paved bed would break,   And take her hence in horror.
translation: If she kneels and asks for mercy for him, her brother's ghost would come back to haunt her and steal her away in horror.

original: Isabel,   Sweet Isabel, do yet but kneel by me;   Hold up your hands, say nothing; I'll speak all.
translation: Isabella, sweet Isabella, just kneel with me. Hold up your hands—you don't have to say anything. I'll do all the talking.

original: They say, best men are moulded out of faults;   And, for the most, become much more the better   For being a little bad: so may my husband.
translation: [To DUKE VINCENTIO]  They say that even the best men make mistakes. And most of them are actually better for having a little imperfection in them. My husband's just the same.

original: O Isabel, will you not lend a knee?
translation: [To ISABELLA]  Oh, Isabella, won't you kneel with me?

original: He dies for Claudio's death.
translation: He dies for Claudio's death.

original: Most bounteous sir,   Look, if it please you, on this man condemn'd,   As if my brother lived:
translation: Generous sir, please treat this condemned man the way you would treat my brother if he were still alive

original: I partly think   A due sincerity govern'd his deeds,   Till he did look on me:
translation: . I partially think that he acted sincerely before he met me.

original: since it is so,   Let him not die. My brother had but justice,   In that he did the thing for which he died:
translation: Since that's the case, don't let him die. My brother got his justice—he did the thing for which he died.

original: For Angelo,   His act did not o'ertake his bad intent,   And must be buried but as an intent
translation: But Angelo, he didn't do the thing that he intended.

original: That perish'd by the way: thoughts are no subjects;   Intents but merely thoughts.
translation: Since it was only an intention, we should forget about it. Thoughts aren't actions; intentions are just thoughts.

original: Merely, my lord.
translation: Just thoughts, my lord.

original: Your suit's unprofitable; stand up, I say.   I have bethought me of another fault.
translation: Your request is useless. Stand up, now. I just thought of another mistake.

original: Provost, how came it Claudio was beheaded   At an unusual hour?
translation: Provost, why was it that Claudio was beheaded at such an unusual time?

original: It was commanded so.
translation: That's what I was commanded to do.

original: Had you a special warrant for the deed?
translation: Did you have a special warrant for it?

original: No, my good lord; it was by private message.
translation: No, my good lord. It was in a private message.

original: For which I do discharge you of your office: Give up your keys.
translation: For that, you're fired from your position. Give me your keys.

original: Pardon me, noble lord:   I thought it was a fault, but knew it not;
translation: Forgive me, sir. I thought it was a mistake, but I wasn't sure.

original: Yet did repent me, after more advice;
translation: I repented after I'd talked with someone about it.

original: For testimony whereof, one in the prison,   That should by private order else have died,   I have reserved alive.
translation: A man in the prison—who should have died, but I kept alive—can testify to it.

original: What's he?
translation: Who's that?

original: His name is Barnardine.
translation: His name is Barnadine.

original: I would thou hadst done so by Claudio. Go fetch him hither; let me look upon him.
translation: I wish you would have kept Claudio alive. Bring him here; let me see him.

original: I am sorry, one so learned and so wise   As you, Lord Angelo, have still appear'd,   Should slip so grossly, both in the heat of blood.
translation: Lord Angelo, I'm sad to see that someone as educated and wise as you, —and who seemed good—would mess up so badly, and let his desires get the best of him.

original: And lack of temper'd judgment afterward.
translation: And then to have had such poor judgment afterward.

original: I am sorry that such sorrow I procure:
translation: I'm sorrow that I've caused so much suffering.

original: And so deep sticks it in my penitent heart   That I crave death more willingly than mercy;   'Tis my deserving, and I do entreat it.
translation: I feel it so painfully in my remorseful heart that I want death more than I want mercy. It's what I deserve; it's what I ask for.

original: Which is that Barnardine?
translation: Which one is Barnadine?

original: This, my lord.
translation: This one, sir.

original: There was a friar told me of this man.
translation: A friar told me about this man.

original: Sirrah, thou art said to have a stubborn soul.   That apprehends no further than this world,   And squarest thy life according.
translation: [To BARNADINE]  Sir, I've heard that you have a stubborn soul; that you don't care about the afterlife and live your life accordingly.

original: Thou'rt condemn'd:   But, for those earthly faults, I quit them all;
translation: You're condemned. But, despite all of your earthly faults, I pardon you.

original: And pray thee take this mercy to provide   For better times to come.
translation: Please take advantage of this mercy to improve your life in the future.

original: Friar, advise him;   I leave him to your hand.
translation: [To FRIAR PETER]  Friar, speak with him; I leave him to you.

original: What muffled fellow's that?
translation: [To the PROVOST]  Who's the man with the bag on his head?

original: This is another prisoner that I saved.   Who should have died when Claudio lost his head;
translation: This is another prisoner that I saved. He should have died when Claudio lost his head,

original: As like almost to Claudio as himself.   [Unmuffles CLAUDIO]
translation: and looks as much like Claudio as Claudio himself.  [He takes the bag off CLAUDIO's head]

original: [To ISABELLA]   If he be like your brother, for his sake   Is he pardon'd; and, for your lovely sake,   Give me your hand and say you will be mine.   He is my brother too: but fitter time for that.
translation: [To ISABELLA]  If he looks like your brother, then I'll pardon him for his sake. And as for your beautiful sake, give me your hand and say you'll be mine. He's my brother, too—or will be soon.

original: By this Lord Angelo perceives he's safe;   Methinks I see a quickening in his eye.
translation: Lord Angelo can tell that he's safe now; I can see the look in his eye.

original: Well, Angelo, your evil quits you well:   Look that you love your wife; her worth worth yours.
translation: [To ANGELO]  Well, Angelo, you're not evil anymore. Make sure you love your wife, and that you're good enough to deserve her.

original: I find an apt remission in myself;   And yet here's one in place I cannot pardon.
translation: And yet, there's one person here who I can't pardon.

original: [To LUCIO]   You, sirrah, that knew me for a fool, a  coward,   One all of luxury, an ass, a madman;
translation: [To LUCIO]  You, sir. You called me an idiot, a coward, wasteful, an ass, crazy.

original: Wherein have I so deserved of you,   That you extol me thus?
translation: What did I do to deserve what you've said about me?

original: 'Faith, my lord. I spoke it but according to the   trick. If you will hang me for it, you may;
translation: Truly, my lord, I only said it as a joke. You can hang me for it if you want.

original: but I   had rather it would please you I might be whipt.
translation: But I'd rather just get whipped, if it would please you, sir.

original: Whipt first, sir, and hanged after.
translation: Whipped first, and hanged afterward.

original: Proclaim it, provost, round about the city.
translation: [To the PROVOST]  Announce it all around the city, Provost.

original: Is any woman wrong'd by this lewd fellow,   As I have heard him swear himself there's one   Whom he begot with child, let her appear,   And he shall marry her:
translation: If any woman has been wronged by this nasty man—since I've heard him swear he got one pregnant—bring her here, and he'll marry her.

original: the nuptial finish'd,   Let him be whipt and hang'd.
translation: After the wedding, have him whipped and hanged.

original: I beseech your highness, do not marry me to a whore. Your highness said even now, I made you a duke: good my lord, do not recompense me in making me a  cuckold.
Upon mine honour, thou shalt marry her.
translation: I swear on my honor—you'll marry her.

original: Thy slanders I forgive; and therewithal   Remit thy other forfeits.
translation: I forgive your slander and pardon all your other crimes, too.

original: Take him to prison;   And see our pleasure herein executed.
translation: Take him to prison and make sure my instructions are executed.

original: Marrying a punk, my lord, is pressing to death, whipping, and hanging.
translation: My lord, marrying a prostitute is worse than being pressed to death, whipped, and hanged.

original: Slandering a prince deserves it.
translation: That's what you deserve for slandering a prince.

original: She, Claudio, that you wrong'd, look you restore.
translation: [To CLAUDIO]  Marry the woman you wronged, Claudio.

original: Joy to you, Mariana! Love her, Angelo:
translation: [To MARIANA]  Best wishes to you, Mariana!

original: I have confess'd her and I know her virtue.
translation: [To ANGELO]  Love her, Angelo. I've heard her confessions and know how good she is.

original: Thanks, good friend Escalus, for thy much goodness:   There's more behind that is more gratulate.
translation: [To ESCALUS]  Thank you for your good friendship, Escalus. There's more congratulations to come.

original: Thanks, provost, for thy care and secrecy:   We shill employ thee in a worthier place.
translation: [To the PROVOST]  Thank you for being so careful and for keeping everything secret, Provost. I'll give you a promotion.

original: Forgive him, Angelo, that brought you home   The head of Ragozine for Claudio's:   The offence pardons itself.
translation: [To ANGELO]  Forgive the sheriff for bringing you Ragozine's head in place of Claudio's, Angelo. The offense pardons itself.

original: Dear Isabel,   I have a motion much imports your good;   Whereto if you'll a willing ear incline,   What's mine is yours and what is yours is mine.
translation: [To ISABELLA]  Dear Isabella, I have something in mind that will benefit you, if you're willing to listen: what's mine is yours and what's yours is mine.

original: So, bring us to our palace; where we'll show   What's yet behind, that's meet you all should know.
translation: [To the crowd]  So, let's go to my palace. I'll explain everything that's still unsaid and that you all should know.

original: To sing a song that old was sung,   From ashes ancient Gower is come;   Assuming man's infirmities,   To glad your ear, and please your eyes.
translation: I'm  John Gower , and I've come back to life (taking on the form of my weak body once again) to tell you an old story that never fails to please the ear and the eye.

original: It hath been sung at festivals,   On ember-eves and holy-ales;   And lords and ladies in their lives   Have read it for restoratives:
translation: It's been told at parties, around the fire, over beers, and in storybooks for generations; men and women have read it to make themselves feel better.

original: The purchase is to make men glorious;   Et bonum quo antiquius, eo melius.
translation: The point is to teach you how to be a better person. You know what they say: "the older and better the story, the better it makes you."

original: If you, born in these latter times,   When wit's more ripe, accept my rhymes.   And that to hear an old man sing   May to your wishes pleasure bring   I life would wish, and that I might   Waste it for you, like taper-light.
translation: And if you modern people (who are more clever than we used to be) will bear with my old-fashioned way of rhyming, you might enjoy what I, an old man, will bring to life on this stage by  candlelight .

original: This Antioch, then, Antiochus the Great   Built up, this city, for his chiefest seat:   The fairest in all Syria,
translation: This is Antioch, a city built by the great King Antiochus to be the most beautiful in Syria, and his capital.

original: I tell you what mine authors say:   This king unto him took a fere,   Who died and left a female heir,   So buxom, blithe, and full of face,   As heaven had lent her all his grace;
translation: According to my sources, the king got married, but his wife died young, leaving him a beautiful, obedient daughter, blessed by the gods.

original: With whom the father liking took,   And her to incest did provoke:   Bad child; worse father!
translation: The king took a liking to her, and forced her to commit incest. Bad girl! Evil father!

original: to entice his own   To evil should be done by none:   But custom what they did begin   Was with long use account no sin.
translation: No one should do such a thing to their own child. Of course, by the time our story begins, they'd been up to it for so long that they forgot it was wrong.

original: The beauty of this sinful dame   Made many princes thither frame,   To seek her as a bed-fellow,   In marriage-pleasures play-fellow:
translation: Princes came from miles around to seek the princess's hand in marriage, hoping to make her their lifelong bedfellow.

original: Which to prevent he made a law,   To keep her still, and men in awe,   That whoso ask'd her for his wife,   His riddle told not, lost his life:
translation: To prevent losing his daughter, the king made a law: whoever wanted to marry the princess would have to answer a riddle, and a wrong answer meant sudden death.

original: So for her many a wight did die,   As yon grim looks do testify.   What now ensues, to the judgment of your eye   I give, my cause who best can justify.
translation: Many poor men lost their lives that way, in pursuit of her, as you can see by the serious looks on their faces. What comes next I'll let you see for yourself; you can be the judge of why.

original: Young prince of Tyre, you have at large received The danger of the task you undertake.
translation: So, Prince of Tyre: you understand how dangerous the task you're about to attempt is?

original: I have, Antiochus, and, with a soul Embolden'd with the glory of her praise, Think death no hazard in this enterprise.
translation: I do, Antiochus. But your daughter is so beautiful that I wouldn't mind if I died trying to win the right to marry her.

original: Bring in our daughter, clothed like a bride,   For the embracements even of Jove himself;
translation: Bring in my daughter. Put her in a wedding dress good enough for the  king  of the  gods  himself.

original: At whose conception, till Lucina reign'd,   Nature this dowry gave, to glad her presence,   The senate-house of planets all did sit,
translation: From the time she was conceived to the time she was  born,   Nature  worked to make her beautiful specifically for this moment of  marriage ,

original: To knit in her their best perfections.
translation: and the whole universe decided to make her as perfect as possible.

original: See where she comes, apparell'd like the spring,   Graces her subjects, and her thoughts the king   Of every virtue gives renown to men!
translation: Here she comes! She's as young and beautiful as the spring. She's kind to her subjects, and her noble, virtuous thoughts are well-regarded by all.

original: Her face the book of praises, where is read   Nothing but curious pleasures, as from thence   Sorrow were ever razed and testy wrath   Could never be her mild companion.
translation: Just the sight of her face makes me happy—it's like all sadness and anger evaporate in her presence.

original: You gods that made me man, and sway in love,   That have inflamed desire in my breast   To taste the fruit of yon celestial tree,   Or die in the adventure,
translation: The gods that created me gave me the uncontrollable  desire  to either be with her or die trying.

original: be my helps,   As I am son and servant to your will,   To compass such a boundless happiness!
translation: Since I'm obedient to the gods, I pray they'll help me secure my future happiness!

original: Prince Pericles,—
translation: Prince Pericles—

original: That would be son to great Antiochus.
translation: —who has every intention of being your son-in-law—

original: Before thee stands this fair Hesperides,   With golden fruit, but dangerous to be touch'd;

For death-like dragons here affright thee hard:   Her face, like heaven, enticeth thee to view   Her countless glory, which desert must gain;   And which, without desert, because thine eye   Presumes to reach, all thy whole heap must die.
Yon sometimes famous princes, like thyself,   Drawn by report, adventurous by desire,
translation: [He points to a pile of skeletons]   Those former princes, like you, were drawn here by the rumors. They were looking for adventure, too.

original: Tell thee, with speechless tongues and semblance pale,   That without covering, save yon field of stars,   Here they stand martyrs, slain in Cupid's wars;
translation: As you can see by their silence (and their bare bones), they're all casualties of love with no grave to speak of, except the stars above.

original: And with dead cheeks advise thee to desist   For going on death's net, whom none resist.
translation: Take a hint from their corpses and turn back now before it's too late.

original: Antiochus, I thank thee, who hath taught   My frail mortality to know itself,
translation: Thanks, Antiochus, for reminding me of my own mortality.

original: And by those fearful objects to prepare   This body, like to them, to what I must;
translation: Those frightening things are preparing my body, like theirs, for the worst that could happen:

original: For death remember'd should be like a mirror,   Who tells us life's but breath, to trust it error.
translation: death.  When we remember death, it should act like a mirror, reflecting back to us the truth that life is short, and that it's a mistake to put our faith in it.

original: I'll make my will then, and, as sick men do   Who know the world, see heaven, but, feeling woe,   Gripe not at earthly joys as erst they did;
translation: I'll make my will, then, like sick men do when they've experienced the world and, near death, are both sad and resigned to give up the joys experienced on earth.

original: So I bequeath a happy peace to you   And all good men, as every prince should do;   My riches to the earth from whence they came;
translation: I wish the best to you and to all good men (as every prince should do), and give away all my belongings.

original: Scorning advice, read the conclusion then:   Which read and not expounded, 'tis decreed,
translation: Since you won't listen to my advice, you'll have to face the consequences: if you read the riddle and can't answer it,

original: As these before thee thou thyself shalt bleed.
translation: you'll be killed like the others before you.

original: Of all say'd yet, mayst thou prove prosperous! Of all say'd yet, I wish thee happiness!
translation: Of all the men who've tried, I hope you succeed! I hope this ends well for you!

original: Like a bold champion, I assume the lists,   Nor ask advice of any other thought   But faithfulness and courage.
translation: Like a knight going into a tournament, the only advice or help I need is faithfulness and courage.

original: I am no viper, yet I feed   On mother's flesh which did me breed.
translation: [Reading the riddle from a scroll]   I'm not a snake, but I eat My own mother's  flesh.

original: I sought a husband, in which labour   I found that kindness in a father:
translation: When I looked for a husband,  I found him in a father.

original: He's father, son, and husband mild;   I mother, wife, and yet his child.
translation: He's father, son, and husband;  I'm mother, wife, and child.

original: How they may be, and yet in two,   As you will live, resolve it you.
translation: How is this possible?  I leave it up to you.

original: Sharp physic is the last: but, O you powers   That give heaven countless eyes to view men's acts,   Why cloud they not their sights perpetually,   If this be true, which makes me pale to read it?
translation: [Looking back up]  Oh, that last part is a bitter pill to swallow. Oh, you gods that see everything we do on earth, how can you look down on such a horrible thing (if what I'm reading is true)?

original: Fair glass of light, I loved you, and could still,   Were not this glorious casket stored with ill:
translation: [He grabs ANTIOCHUS's DAUGHTER's hand]  Beautiful princess, I did love you,  and would still love you, but now I know the dark secret behind that pretty face.

original: But I must tell you, now my thoughts revolt   For he's no man on whom perfections wait   That, knowing sin within, will touch the gate.
translation: I have to tell you: all my plans are unravelling, because a good man could hardly marry into such a depraved situation once he knows what's in store.

original: You are a fair viol, and your sense the strings;   Who, finger'd to make man his lawful music,   Would draw heaven down, and all the gods, to hearken:
translation: You're  gorgeous  and your character makes you even more desirable; under normal circumstances, anyone would be lucky to marry you, and the gods would smile down on it.

original: But being play'd upon before your time,   Hell only danceth at so harsh a chime.   Good sooth, I care not for you.
translation: But you've been violated so young; it's a  crime  worthy of hell.  I'm not interested in you at all.

original: Prince Pericles, touch not, upon thy life.   For that's an article within our law,
translation: Don't touch her, Prince Pericles, if you value your life. That's the law, and it's as dangerous as the rest.

original: As dangerous as the rest. Your time's expired:   Either expound now, or receive your sentence.
translation: Your time is up! Tell us the answer now, or prepare to die.

original: Great king,   Few love to hear the sins they love to act;   'Twould braid yourself too near for me to tell it.
translation: Sir, no one likes to hear their sins repeated back to them—it would offend you to hear me say it.

original: Who has a book of all that monarchs do,   He's more secure to keep it shut than shown:
translation: Anyone who found out about this before probably kept their mouth shut rather than telling.

original: For vice repeated is like the wandering wind.   Blows dust in other's eyes, to spread itself;   And yet the end of all is bought thus dear,   The breath is gone, and the sore eyes see clear:   To stop the air would hurt them.
translation: Evil spreads as quickly as dust on the wind.  As the dust surrounds us and blinds us, we can no longer tell it's there; we start to think it's normal.

original: The blind mole casts   Copp'd hills towards heaven, to tell the earth is  throng'd   By man's oppression; and the poor worm doth die for't.
translation: The blind mole throws his hills of dirt toward heaven, to tell the gods the earth is filled with man's evil, and the worm dies because of it .

original: Kings are earth's gods; in vice their law's their will;   And if Jove stray, who dares say Jove doth ill?
translation: The world is full of evil men like you, but kings are supposed to be gods on earth!  When kings are corrupt, they can twist the law to conform to their evil desires (and when a god makes a mistake, who would dare to tell him?).

original: It is enough you know; and it is fit,   What being more known grows worse, to smother it.
translation: You know your actions are wrong, and the fact that you know and still keep on doing it makes it even worse.

original: All love the womb that their first being bred,   Then give my tongue like leave to love my head.
translation: By the  love everyone has for their own mother,  please don't kill me for what I've said!

original: Heaven, that I had thy head! he has found   the meaning:   But I will gloze with him.
translation: I wish I had a mind like yours! He's figured out the meaning, but I'll talk him out of it.

original: —   Young prince of Tyre,   Though by the tenor of our strict edict,   Your exposition misinterpreting,
translation: Prince of Tyre: though, according to our law, I could kill you for not giving me a correct answer,

original: We might proceed to cancel of your days;   Yet hope, succeeding from so fair a tree   As your fair self, doth tune us otherwise:
translation: I'll give you some more time on account of your noble blood and your way with words.

original: Forty days longer we do respite you;   If by which time our secret be undone,   This mercy shows we'll joy in such a son:   And until then your entertain shall be   As doth befit our honour and your worth.
translation: If, in forty days' time, you reveal the secret, I'll welcome you as my son-in-law with a celebratory feast worthy of myself as a king and you as a prince.

original: How courtesy would seem to cover sin,   When what is done is like an hypocrite,   The which is good in nothing but in sight!
translation: You're trying to hide your evil with a show of hospitality, but it's hypocrisy; it only looks good from the outside!

original: If it be true that I interpret false,   Then were it certain you were not so bad   As with foul incest to abuse your soul;
translation: If I'd really gotten the answer wrong, then that would mean you weren't dirtying your soul by committing disgusting incest.

original: Where now you're both a father and a son,   By your untimely claspings with your child,   Which pleasure fits an husband, not a father;
translation: But now, by sleeping with your daughter, you're both father and son, acting more like a husband than a father . . .

original: And she an eater of her mother's flesh,   By the defiling of her parent's bed;   And both like serpents are, who though they feed   On sweetest flowers, yet they poison breed.
translation: and she's filling the role her mother should, taking her mother's place in your bed. They're both like  snakes  who eat pretty flowers but produce deadly poison.

original: Antioch, farewell! for wisdom sees, those men   Blush not in actions blacker than the night,   Will shun no course to keep them from the light.
translation: Goodbye, Antioch! I'm smart enough to know that a guy who's comfortable doing one evil thing won't hesitate to do another one if it'll keep him from being found out.
