original: And not your knowledge, your personal pain, but even   Your purse, still open, hath built Lord Cerimon   Such strong renown as time shall ne'er decay.
translation: Not only your knowledge and your personal effort, but also your charity, Lord Cerimon, have built a reputation that will last forever.

original: So; lift there.
translation: Put it up there.

original: What is that?
translation: What is that?

original: Sir, even now Did the sea toss upon our shore this chest: 'Tis of some wreck.
translation: Sir, this chest washed up on the shore from a shipwreck.

original: Set 't down, let's look upon't.
translation: Set it down; let's look at it.

original: 'Tis like a coffin, sir.
translation: It looks like a coffin, sir.

original: Whate'er it be,   'Tis wondrous heavy.
translation: Whatever it is, it's very heavy.

original: Wrench it open straight:   If the sea's stomach be o'ercharged with gold,   'Tis a good constraint of fortune it belches upon us.
translation: Open it up quick! If there's too much gold laying on the  ocean floor , it's good luck that the sea has thrown it up to us.

original: 'Tis so, my lord.
translation: Of course, sir.

original: How close 'tis caulk'd and bitumed! Did the sea cast it up?
translation: It's really sealed up tight! Did it come out of the sea?

original: I never saw so huge a billow, sir, As toss'd it upon shore.
translation: The biggest wave I've ever seen washed it up on the shore.

original: Wrench it open; Soft! it smells most sweetly in my sense.
translation: Open it!  Shh! I smell something sweet.

original: A delicate odour.
translation: A delicate odor.

original: As ever hit my nostril. So, up with it. O you most potent gods! what's here? a corse!
translation: The most delicate I've ever smelled. Lift up the lid! Oh, you powerful gods! What's in here?  A body!

original: Most strange!
translation: How strange!

original: Shrouded in cloth of state; balm'd and entreasured   With full bags of spices! A passport too!   Apollo, perfect me in the characters!
translation: Wearing royal clothes, scented with perfumes and spices! With a passport, too!  Apollo , help me read what this says.

original: [Reading from a scroll]   'Here I give to understand,   If e'er this coffin drive a-land,   I, King Pericles, have lost   This queen, worth all our mundane cost.
translation: [ He picks up a scroll and reads from it]   "To whoever's reading this, if this coffin ever comes to land: I, King Pericles, have lost my beloved wife.

original: Who finds her, give her burying;   She was the daughter of a king:   Besides this treasure for a fee,   The gods requite his charity!'
translation: If you've found her, please give her a proper burial. She was the daughter of the king. Take this gold as payment for your service. May the gods bless you!"

original: If thou livest, Pericles, thou hast a heart   That even cracks for woe! This chanced tonight.
translation: [To the absent Pericles]  Pericles, if you're alive, I feel sorry for you. She must have died tonight.

original: Most likely, sir.
translation: Most likely, sir.

original: Nay, certainly to-night;   For look how fresh she looks! They were too rough   That threw her in the sea.
translation: No, definitely tonight, look how fresh she looks! They shouldn't have thrown her in the sea.

original: Make a fire within:   Fetch hither all my boxes in my closet.
translation: Build a fire inside, and bring all the boxes from my closet.

original: Death may usurp on nature many hours,   And yet the fire of life kindle again   The o'erpress'd spirits.
translation: It may look like someone is dead for hours, but then they revive and come back to life.

original: I heard of an Egyptian   That had nine hours lien dead,   Who was by good appliance recovered.
translation: I heard of an Egyptian who was dead for nine hours and then, with some help, recovered.

original: Well said, well said; the fire and cloths.   The rough and woeful music that we have,   Cause it to sound, beseech you.
translation: [To the servants]  Perfect, perfect. Give me the fire and the clothes. Play some sad music, please!

original: The viol once more: how thou stirr'st, thou block!   The music there!—   I pray you, give her air.
Gentlemen.   This queen will live: nature awakes; a warmth   Breathes out of her:
translation: [To the GENTLEMEN]  Gentlemen. The queen will live. Look, she's waking up! She's warm!

original: she hath not been entranced   Above five hours: see how she gins to blow   Into life's flower again!
translation: She's been asleep for about five hours, but look how she  comes back to life !

original: The heavens, Through you, increase our wonder and set up Your fame forever.
translation: The gods, through you, amaze us. You've secured your fame forever.

original: She is alive; behold,   Her eyelids, cases to those heavenly jewels   Which Pericles hath lost,   Begin to part their fringes of bright gold;
translation: She's alive! Look, her eyelids, which cover the  beautiful eyes  which Pericles has lost, are just beginning to separate their eyelashes.

original: The diamonds of a most praised water   Do appear, to make the world twice rich.
translation: Now her sparkling eyes are appearing— and what a treasure they are.

original: Live,   And make us weep to hear your fate, fair creature,   Rare as you seem to be.
translation: [To THAISA]  Live, and bring tears to our eyes with your sad story, beautiful lady. We can tell how special you are.

original: O dear Diana, Where am I? Where's my lord? What world is this?
Is not this strange?
translation: Isn't this strange?

original: Most rare.
translation: Very odd.

original: Hush, my gentle neighbours!   Lend me your hands; to the next chamber bear her.
translation: Quiet, gentlemen! Please, pick her up and take her into the next room.

original: Get linen: now this matter must be look'd to,   For her relapse is mortal. Come, come;   And AEsculapius guide us!
translation: Get some sheets; we need to hurry, since a relapse could kill her. Come, come, and  Aesculapius  help us!

original: Most honour'd Cleon, I must needs be gone;   My twelve months are expired, and Tyrus stands   In a litigious peace.
translation: Dear Cleon, I have to go. My year is up and the state of peace in Tyre is fragile.

original: You, and your lady,   Take from my heart all thankfulness! The gods   Make up the rest upon you!
translation: Thanks for everything you and your wife have done for me. May the gods bless you.

original: Your shafts of fortune, though they hurt you mortally, Yet glance full wanderingly on us.
O your sweet queen! That the strict fates had pleased you had brought her  hither, To have bless'd mine eyes with her!
We cannot but obey   The powers above us.
translation: We have to obey the gods above.

original: Could I rage and roar   As doth the sea she lies in, yet the end   Must be as 'tis.
translation: I can rage as loud as the sea and it won't bring Thaisa back.

original: My gentle babe Marina, whom,   For she was born at sea, I have named so, here   I charge your charity withal, leaving her   The infant of your care;
translation: I named our daughter Marina because she was born at sea. Please, I'm asking a favor: I'm leaving the baby in your care.

original: beseeching you   To give her princely training, that she may be   Manner'd as she is born.
translation: Make sure she has an education fit for a princess, so she grows up to be as cultivated as her pedigree.

original: Fear not, my lord, but think   Your grace, that fed my country with your corn,   For which the people's prayers still fall upon you,   Must in your child be thought on.
translation: Don't worry, sir. You provided corn for my country when we were starving. My people still pray for you, and we'll take care of your child, too.

original: If neglection   Should therein make me vile, the common body,   By you relieved, would force me to my duty:
translation: If I neglected my duty, the common people (whom you saved) would force me to do my duty.

original: But if to that my nature need a spur,   The gods revenge it upon me and mine,   To the end of generation!
translation: But if I need any punishment, may the gods take revenge on me and my descendants of the next generation!

original: I believe you;   Your honour and your goodness teach me to't,   Without your vows.
translation: I believe. Your actions speak louder than your words; you don't have to swear.

original: Till she be married, madam,   By bright Diana, whom we honour, all   Unscissor'd shall this hair of mine remain,   Though I show ill in't. So I take my leave.
translation: I won't cut my hair again until she gets married, though it might look strange. Goodbye.

original: Good madam, make me blessed in your care   In bringing up my child.
translation: [To DIONYZA]  Ma'am, please take good care of my child.

original: I have one myself, Who shall not be more dear to my respect Than yours, my lord.
translation: I have a daughter, too. I'll love yours like my own.

original: Madam, my thanks and prayers.
translation: You have my thanks and prayers, ma'am.

original: We'll bring your grace e'en to the edge o' the shore, Then give you up to the mask'd Neptune and The gentlest winds of heaven.
I will embrace   Your offer.
translation: I'll accept that offer.

original: Come, dearest madam.
translation: [To MARINA]  Come here, sweetheart.  [He holds the baby]

original: O, no tears,   Lychorida, no tears:   Look to your little mistress, on whose grace   You may depend hereafter.
translation: Don't cry, Lychorida. Take care of your little mistress; she'll be in charge of you when I'm gone.

original: Come, my lord.
translation: [To CLEON]  Let's go, sir.

original: Madam, this letter, and some certain jewels, Lay with you in your coffer: which are now At your command. Know you the character?
translation: Ma'am, this letter and some jewelry were in your coffin with you. Here they are; they're yours. Do you recognize the handwriting?

original: It is my lord's.   That I was shipp'd at sea, I well remember,   Even on my eaning time;
translation: It's my husband's. I remember being set in the sea right after I gave birth,

original: but whether there   Deliver'd, by the holy gods,   I cannot rightly say.
translation: but don't know how I washed up here.

original: But since King Pericles,   My wedded lord, I ne'er shall see again,   A vestal livery will I take me to,   And never more have joy.
translation: Since I'll never see my husband, King Pericles, again, I'll become a nun and will never be happy again.

original: Madam, if this you purpose as ye speak,   Diana's temple is not distant far,
translation: If you mean it, ma'am, Diana's temple is nearby.

original: Where you may abide till your date expire.
translation: You can stay there for the rest of your life.

original: Moreover, if you please, a niece of mine   Shall there attend you.
translation: Furthermore, my niece can take you there if you like.

original: My recompense is thanks, that's all; Yet my good will is great, though the gift small.
translation: Thank you. I wish I had more to repay your kindness.

original: Thy oath remember; thou hast sworn to do't:   'Tis but a blow, which never shall be known.
translation: Remember your promise: you've sworn to do it. It's just a little thing which no one will ever find out about.

original: Thou canst not do a thing in the world so soon,   To yield thee so much profit.
translation: And you can count on being rewarded.

original: Let not conscience,   Which is but cold, inflaming love i' thy bosom,   Inflame too nicely;
translation: Don't let your icy conscience thaw out with the heat of love.

original: nor let pity, which   Even women have cast off, melt thee, but be   A soldier to thy purpose.
translation: And don't let pity, which even women have nothing to do with, get the best of you— do just what I've told you to do.

original: I will do't; but yet she is a goodly creature.
translation: I'll do it, but she is an innocent girl.

original: The fitter, then, the gods should have her. Here she comes weeping for her only mistress' death. Thou art resolved?
translation: It's better, then, that the gods should have her. Here she comes, crying over Lychorida's death. Are you ready?

original: I am resolved.
translation: I'm ready.

original: No, I will rob Tellus of her weed,   To strew thy green with flowers: the yellows, blues,   The purple violets, and marigolds,
translation: I'll take every flower  Mother Earth  has to offer, to decorate your grave with yellows, blues, purple violets, marigolds—

original: Shall as a carpet hang upon thy grave,   While summer-days do last.
translation: all these will cover you as long as summer lasts.

original: Ay me! poor maid,   Born in a tempest, when my mother died,   This world to me is like a lasting storm,   Whirring me from my friends.
translation: Poor me! When I was born (in a storm), my mother died; my whole life has been a continuous storm blowing me away from my friends.

original: How now, Marina! why do you keep alone?   How chance my daughter is not with you?
translation: Hello, Marina! Why are you alone? Why isn't my daughter with you?

original: Do not   Consume your blood with sorrowing: you have   A nurse of me. Lord, how your favour's changed   With this unprofitable woe!
translation: Don't make yourself sick with being so upset; I'll be your nurse now. Look how your situation has changed with this unfortunate loss!

original: Come, give me your flowers, ere the sea mar it.   Walk with Leonine; the air is quick there,   And it pierces and sharpens the stomach.
translation: Come on, give me your flowers before the sea air wilts them. Walk with Leonine down by the shore. The air will do you some good; the wind is refreshing and makes your stomach strong.

original: Come,   Leonine, take her by the arm, walk with her.
translation: Come on, Leonine; take her by the arm, walk with her.

original: No, I pray you; I'll not bereave you of your servant.
translation: No, please. I won't take your servant from you.

original: Come, come;   I love the king your father, and yourself,   With more than foreign heart.
translation: Come, come! I love you and your father as if I were his own subject rather than a foreigner.

original: We every day   Expect him here: when he shall come and find   Our paragon to all reports thus blasted,
translation: We expect him to visit any day now, and when he does, what will he say when he finds our little princess in poor health?

original: He will repent the breadth of his great voyage;   Blame both my lord and me, that we have taken   No care to your best courses.
translation: He'll wish he hadn't come so far, and he'll blame my husband and me for not taking care of you like we promised to do.

original: Go, I pray you,   Walk, and be cheerful once again; reserve   That excellent complexion, which did steal   The eyes of young and old.
translation: Go, please. Walk, be happy, bring back those rosy cheeks we all love so much!

original: Care not for me   I can go home alone.
translation: Don't worry about me; I can go home alone.

original: Well, I will go; But yet I have no desire to it.
translation: Well, I'll go even though I don't want to.

original: Come, come, I know 'tis good for you. Walk half an hour, Leonine, at the least: Remember what I have said.
translation: Come, come! I know it's best for you. Walk half an hour, Leonine, at least. Remember what I said.

original: I warrant you, madam.
translation: Of course, ma'am.

original: I'll leave you, my sweet lady, for a while: Pray, walk softly, do not heat your blood: What! I must have a care of you.
translation: I'll leave you for a while, dear. Mind you, walk slowly and don't get too worked up! What? I have to take care of you!

original: My thanks, sweet madam.
translation: Thanks, ma'am.

original: Is this wind westerly that blows?
translation: Is that a west wind blowing?

original: South-west.
translation: South-west.

original: When I was born, the wind was north.
translation: When I was born, the wind was from the north.

original: Was't so?
translation: Was it?

original: My father, as nurse said, did never fear,   But cried 'Good seaman!' to the sailors, galling   His kingly hands, haling ropes;
translation: According to my nurse, my father wasn't afraid. He just called out to the sailors, "Good seamen!" and helped them, pulling the ropes with his own hands,

original: And, clasping to the mast, endured a sea   That almost burst the deck.
translation: and holding onto the mast to ride out the waves that almost broke the ship.

original: When was this?
translation: When was this?

original: When I was born:   Never was waves nor wind more violent;   And from the ladder-tackle washes off   A canvas-climber.
translation: When I was born. The waves and wind were incredibly violent, washing a sailor straight out of the crow's nest.

original: 'Ha!' says one, 'wilt out?'   And with a dropping industry they skip   From stem to stern:
translation: Another sailor said, "Ha! Will this ever end?" and they kept running around from the front to the back of the boat,

original: the boatswain whistles, and   The master calls, and trebles their confusion.
translation: the  boatswain  whistling, the master calling, and everything in complete chaos.

original: Come, say your prayers.
translation: Say your prayers, now.

original: What mean you?
translation: What do you mean?

original: If you require a little space for prayer,   I grant it: pray; but be not tedious,
translation: If you need a little room to pray, I'll allow it, but don't take too long.

original: For the gods are quick of ear, and I am sworn   To do my work with haste.
translation: The gods might listen, you know, and I swore I'd do my job quickly.

original: Why will you kill me?
translation: Why would you want to kill me?

original: To satisfy my lady.
translation: To satisfy Dionyza.

original: Why would she have me kill'd?   Now, as I can remember, by my troth,   I never did her hurt in all my life:
translation: Why would she want me killed? As far as I can remember, I've never done anything to hurt her in my life.

original: I never spake bad word, nor did ill turn   To any living creature: believe me, la,   I never kill'd a mouse, nor hurt a fly:
translation: I've never said a mean word or done a bad thing to a single living creature. Believe me, I never killed a mouse or even hurt a fly!

original: I trod upon a worm against my will,   But I wept for it.
translation: Once I stepped on a worm on accident, and I cried.

original: How have I offended,   Wherein my death might yield her any profit,   Or my life imply her any danger?
translation: How have I offended her enough that she would want to kill me? How would she gain from my death? How is she threatened by my life?

original: My commission Is not to reason of the deed, but do it.
translation: My job isn't to debate the reason. It's just to do it.

original: You will not do't for all the world, I hope.   You are well favour'd, and your looks foreshow   You have a gentle heart.
translation: You won't do it for anything in the world, I hope. You're handsome; I can tell by your looks that you have a gentle heart.

original: I saw you lately,   When you caught hurt in parting two that fought:   Good sooth, it show'd well in you:
translation: I saw you recently when you got hurt breaking up a fight, and really, it said a lot about your character.

original: do so now:   Your lady seeks my life; come you between,   And save poor me, the weaker.
translation: Do the right thing now! Your lady wants me dead; don't do it. Save poor me, the weaker one.

original: I am sworn, And will dispatch.
translation: I swore I would, so here we go . . .

original: Hold, villain!
translation: Stop right there, you scoundrel!

original: A prize! a prize!
translation: Some booty! Some booty!

original: Half-part, mates, half-part. Come, let's have her aboard suddenly.
translation: Let's split it equally, mates, equally. Come on, get her onboard.

original: These roguing thieves serve the great pirate Valdes;   And they have seized Marina. Let her go:   There's no hope she will return.
translation: Those terrible thieves who've taken Marina serve the great pirate, Valdes. Let her go— there's not a chance of her coming back.

original: I'll swear   she's dead,   And thrown into the sea. But I'll see further:
translation: I'll swear she's dead and that I threw her into the sea . . . actually, I'll follow along and see what happens.

original: Perhaps they will but please themselves upon her,   Not carry her aboard. If she remain,   Whom they have ravish'd must by me be slain.
translation: They might just have their way with her and not take her onboard. If she survives the assault, I'll have to kill her.

original: Boult!
translation: Boult!

original: Sir?
translation: Sir?

original: Search the market narrowly; Mytilene is full of gallants. We lost too much money this mart by being too wenchless.
translation: Search the market carefully. Mytilene is full of young men. We lost too much money this season because we didn't have enough girls.

original: We were never so much out of creatures.
translation: We've never had such a shortage of creatures.

original: We have but   poor three, and they can do no more than they can   do;
translation: We only have three, and they can only do what they can do.

original: and they with continual action are even as good as  rotten.
translation: And they've worked so much they're as  good as rotten.

original: Therefore let's have fresh ones, whate'er we pay for   them.
translation: So, let's get some fresh ones, no matter what we have to pay for them.

original: If there be not a conscience to be used in   every trade, we shall never prosper.
translation: If we don't put any heart into this business we'll never succeed.

original: Thou sayest true: 'tis not our bringing up of poor bastards,—as, I think, I have brought up some eleven—
Ay, to eleven; and brought them down again. But shall I search the market?
What else, man? The stuff we have, a strong wind will blow it to pieces, they are so pitifully sodden.
translation: What else can we do? The girls we have are so pitiful, a strong wind would blow them all to pieces.

original: Thou sayest true; they're too unwholesome, o'   conscience.
translation: You're right; they're a mess, truth be told.

original: The poor Transylvanian is dead, that   lay with the little baggage.
translation: The poor Transylvanian girl is dead—the one that slept with that guy with the tiny junk.

original: Ay, she quickly pooped him; she made him roast-meat for worms. But I'll go search the market.
Three or four thousand chequins were as pretty a proportion to live quietly, and so give over.
translation: Three or four thousand gold coins is all we need to retire quietly and give up the business.

original: Why to give over, I pray you? is it a shame to get when we are old?
translation: Why would we give it up? Is there anything wrong with working while we're old?

original: O, our credit comes not in like the commodity, nor   the commodity wages not with the danger:
translation: Our credit's not as good as our property, and our property hasn't held up well.

original: therefore,   if in our youths we could pick up some pretty   estate, 'twere not amiss to keep our door hatched.
translation: When we were young we could pick up lots of young girls, and it was easy to keep a roof over our heads.

original: Besides, the sore terms we stand upon with the gods   will be strong with us for giving over.
translation: Besides, the fact that we're in the gods' bad books is reason enough to retire.

original: Come, other sorts offend as well as we.
translation: Oh, come on. Loads of people do as much evil as we do.

original: As well as we! ay, and better too; we offend worse.
translation: As much as we do? But our evil is worse.

original: Neither is our profession any trade; it's no   calling. But here comes Boult.
translation: And our profession isn't really a "trade" or a "calling." But here comes Boult.

original: Come your ways. My masters, you say she's a virgin?
translation: Hurry up, now. [To the PIRATES] So, guys, you say she's a virgin?

original: O, sir, we doubt it not.
translation: Oh, sir, we have no doubt.

original: Master, I have gone through for this piece, you see: if you like her, so; if not, I have lost my earnest.
translation: Master, I've paid through the nose for this one. If you like her, good. If not, I've lost my bet.

original: Boult, has she any qualities?
translation: Boult, what are her assets?

original: She has a good face, speaks well, and has excellent good clothes: there's no further necessity of qualities can make her be refused.
translation: She has a good face, speaks well, and has really nice clothes. There's nothing about her that would make you dislike her.

original: What's her price, Boult?
translation: What's her price, Boult?

original: I cannot be bated one doit of a thousand pieces.
translation: I can't get her for a cent less than a thousand gold coins.

original: Well, follow me, my masters, you shall have your   money presently.
translation: Well, follow me, guys. You'll get your money shortly.

original: Wife, take her in; instruct her   what she has to do, that she may not be raw in her   entertainment.
translation: [To BAWD]  Wife, take her in. Teach her what she has to do so she's not caught unawares her first time.

original: Boult, take you the marks of her, the colour of her   hair, complexion, height, age, with warrant of her   virginity; and cry 'He that will give most shall   have her first.'
translation: Boult, write a full report of her: the color of her hair, complexion, height, age, with a guarantee of her virginity, and cry, "Whoever pays the most can have her first."

original: Such a maidenhead were no cheap   thing, if men were as they have been. Get this done   as I command you.
translation: If I know men, a virginity like this won't go cheap. Do exactly as I say.

original: Performance shall follow.
translation: I'll take care of it.

original: Alack that Leonine was so slack, so slow!   He should have struck, not spoke;
translation: If only Leonine hadn't been so slow! He should have killed me instead of talking so much.

original: or that these  pirates,   Not enough barbarous, had not o'erboard thrown me   For to seek my mother!
translation: Or if only the pirates (as if they weren't barbarous enough) had thrown me overboard, to go after my mother!

original: Why lament you, pretty one?
translation: Why are you crying, pretty girl?

original: That I am pretty.
translation: Because I'm pretty.

original: Come, the gods have done their part in you.
translation: Come on, the gods have blessed you.

original: I accuse them not.
translation: I'm not accusing them.

original: You are light into my hands, where you are like to  live.
translation: You've come into my hands now, where you're likely to live.

original: The more my fault To scape his hands where I was like to die.
translation: Which makes it even worse that I escaped Leonine's hands, where I might have died.

original: Ay, and you shall live in pleasure.
translation: Oh, but you'll live in pleasure.

original: No.
translation: No.

translation: Yes, you will, and you'll taste all different kinds of gentlemen. You'll do well! You'll have all sorts. What? Why are you covering your ears?

original: Are you a woman?
translation: Are you a woman?

original: What would you have me be, an I be not a woman?
translation: What would you rather me be, if not a woman?

translation: A good woman, or not a woman at all.

translation: Shut your mouth, girl. I think I'll have to do something about you.

translation: You're  young  and naive and you'll have to be broken as I would have you.

original: The gods defend me!
translation: May the gods protect me!

original: If it please the gods to defend you by men, then men must comfort you, men must feed you, men must stir you up. Boult's returned.
Now, sir, hast thou cried her through the market?
translation: Have you spread the word about her all over the market?

original: I have cried her almost to the number of her hairs; I have drawn her picture with my voice.
translation: I've described her down to every last hair. I've drawn a picture of her with my voice.

original: And I prithee tell me, how dost thou find the inclination of the people, especially of the younger  sort?
translation: And please, tell me: how do people seem to be reacting, especially the younger ones?

original: 'Faith, they listened to me as they would have   hearkened to their father's testament.
translation: Well, they listened to me as closely as they would to their own father's will being read.

original: There was a   Spaniard's mouth so watered, that he went to bed to   her very description.
translation: There was a Spanish guy whose mouth watered so much, he went to masturbate off just the description of her.

original: We shall have him here to-morrow with his best ruff on.
translation: I'm sure he'll be here tomorrow in his best clothes.

original: To-night, to-night. But, mistress, do you know the French knight that cowers i' the hams?
translation: Tonight, tonight. But, mistress, do you know the French guy who works as a butcher?

original: Who, Monsieur Veroles?
Ay, he: he offered to cut a caper at the proclamation; but he made a groan at it, and swore he would see her to-morrow.
Well, well; as for him, he brought his disease   hither: here he does but repair it.
translation: Well, well, as for him— he brought his disease here, and he just keeps it up.

original: I know he will   come in our shadow, to scatter his crowns in the   sun.
translation: I know he'll come here soon and that he'll spend plenty of money.

original: Well, if we had of every nation a traveller, we should lodge them with this sign.
translation: Well, if we had customers from every country in the world, we'd welcome them in, since they either have syphilis or will do soon.

original: [To MARINA]   Pray you, come hither awhile. You   have fortunes coming upon you.
translation: [To MARINA]  Come here for a minute. Good things are coming your way.

original: Mark me: you must   seem to do that fearfully which you commit   willingly, despise profit where you have most gain.
translation: Mark my words: you need to pretend you're afraid of having sex even though you're perfectly willing, and you need to seem like you don't want the money, even though you'll make a fortune.

original: To weep that you live as ye do makes pity in your   lovers: seldom but that pity begets you a good   opinion, and that opinion a mere profit.
translation: If you cry about having to work as a prostitute, your customers will take pity on you; pity equals good reviews, and good reviews equals a huge profit.

original: I understand you not.
translation: I don't understand you.

original: O, take her home, mistress, take her home: these blushes of hers must be quenched with some present  practise.
translation: Oh, take her home, mistress, take her home. We'll get rid of all this shyness with a little practice.

original: Thou sayest true, i' faith, so they must; for your bride goes to that with shame which is her way to go with warrant.
translation: You're right, darn it, we will. Even brides are afraid of the wedding night, though they have no reason to be.

original: 'Faith, some do, and some do not. But, mistress, if I have bargained for the joint,—
translation: Well, some do, some don't. But, mistress, since it's me that bought her—

original: Thou mayst cut a morsel off the spit.
I may so.
translation: I may?

original: Who should deny it? Come, young one, I like the manner of your garments well.
translation: Who's stopping you? Cheer up, missy. I like your clothes.

original: Ay, by my faith, they shall not be changed yet.
translation: Ah, don't change them yet.

original: Boult, spend thou that in the town: report what a   sojourner we have; you'll lose nothing by custom.
translation: [She gives BOULT a coin]  Boult, spread the news in town about our new guest, and don't leave out a single detail.

original: When nature flamed this piece, she meant thee a good   turn; therefore say what a paragon she is, and thou   hast the harvest out of thine own report.
translation: When Mother Nature put together this girl, she meant to do you a favor. If you tell everyone how beautiful she is, you'll get money and you'll get to sleep with her, too.

original: I warrant you, mistress, thunder shall not so awake the beds of eels as my giving out her beauty stir up the lewdly-inclined. I'll bring home some to-night.
translation: I promise I'll excite those dirty-minded men as much as I can. I'll bring some home tonight.

original: Come your ways; follow me.
translation: Come on, then, follow me.

original: If fires be hot, knives sharp, or waters deep, Untied I still my virgin knot will keep. Diana, aid my purpose!
translation: I swear I'll stay a virgin! Diana, help me!

original: What have we to do with Diana? Pray you, will you go  with us?
Why, are you foolish? Can it be undone?
translation: You idiot, why would you ask if I can "undo it?"

original: O Dionyza, such a piece of slaughter The sun and moon ne'er look'd upon!
translation: Dionyza, there's never been such a horrible murder committed on the earth.

original: I think You'll turn a child again.
translation: I think you're about to turn back into a baby!

original: Were I chief lord of all this spacious world,   I'ld give it to undo the deed.
translation: Were I the king of the whole world, I would do anything to undo this.

original: O lady,   Much less in blood than virtue, yet a princess   To equal any single crown o' the earth   I' the justice of compare!
translation: Poor Marina! She was not only a princess by blood, she was a virtuous person, the equal of any single princess on the earth by comparison!

original: O villain Leonine!   Whom thou hast poison'd too:   If thou hadst drunk to him, 't had been a kindness   Becoming well thy fact:
translation: Curse you, Leonine. And you've poisoned him, too, haven't you? If you'd poisoned yourself, it would have been the punishment you deserved.

original: what canst thou say   When noble Pericles shall demand his child?
translation: What are you going to say to Pericles when he comes looking for his child?

original: That she is dead. Nurses are not the fates,   To foster it, nor ever to preserve.
translation: That she's dead. The Fates aren't nurses; they don't protect our lives forever or even for a while.

original: She died at night; I'll say so. Who can cross it?
translation: She died at night; I'll say so. Who would dare to contradict me?

original: Unless you play the pious innocent,   And for an honest attribute cry out   'She died by foul play.'
translation: Unless you try to play Mr. Innocent and, in a display of honesty, blurt out, "She was murdered!"

original: O, go to. Well, well, Of all the faults beneath the heavens, the gods Do like this worst.
translation: Oh, quit it. Well, well, of all the evil things that go on on earth, the gods will be the least happy about this.

original: Be one of those that think   The petty wrens of Tarsus will fly hence,   And open this to Pericles.
translation: You're one of those who thinks a little birdie is going to fly to Tarsus and tell Pericles what happened!

original: I do shame   To think of what a noble strain you are,   And of how coward a spirit.
translation: I'm ashamed to think of what a coward you are, and a king, too.

original: To such proceeding   Who ever but his approbation added,   Though not his prime consent,
translation: Anyone who would have said "yes" to this, even if he didn't do it himself,

original: he did not flow   From honourable sources.
translation: is a bad person.

original: Be it so, then:   Yet none does know, but you, how she came dead,   Nor none can know, Leonine being gone.
translation: So be it. But no one besides you knows how she died— and no one else will know, since Leonine is dead.

original: She did disdain my child, and stood between   Her and her fortunes: none would look on her,   But cast their gazes on Marina's face;
translation: She made my daughter look bad, and stood between her and a good marriage. No one would look at her when Marina was nearby;

original: Whilst ours was blurted at and held a malkin   Not worth the time of day. It pierced me through;
translation: they looked at her face, while our daughter's was criticized and treated as though she wasn't worth the time of day. It hurt me to see that

original: And though you call my course unnatural,   You not your child well loving, yet I find   It greets me as an enterprise of kindness   Perform'd to your sole daughter.
translation: and, though you may criticize me, it strikes me as what a loving parent ought to do for your only daughter.

original: Heavens forgive it!
translation: May the gods forgive you!

original: And as for Pericles,   What should he say? We wept after her hearse,   And yet we mourn: her monument   Is almost finish'd,
translation: And as for Pericles, what can he say? We cried at her funeral, and we mourn now. The monument to her is almost finished.

original: and her epitaphs   In glittering golden characters express   A general praise to her, and care in us   At whose expense 'tis done.
translation: The epitaph on it proclaims how great she was in gold letters. We've done all the right things, and have spared no expense.

original: Thou art like the harpy, Which, to betray, dost, with thine angel's face, Seize with thine eagle's talons.
You are like one that superstitiously Doth swear to the gods that winter kills the flies: But yet I know you'll do as I advise.
translation: You're like a person who superstitiously swears by the gods, but I know you'll do as I say.

original: Did you ever hear the like?
translation: Have you ever heard anything like it?

original: No, nor never shall do in such a place as this, she being once gone.
translation: No. I'll never set foot in a place like this again, if she's not there.

original: But to have divinity preached there! did you ever dream of such a thing?
translation: Isn't it strange to hear such godly preaching there? Did you ever dream of such a thing?

original: No, no. Come, I am for no more bawdy-houses: shall's go hear the vestals sing?
translation: No, no. Listen; I'm not interested in brothels anymore. Should we go hear the nuns sing?

original: I'll do any thing now that is virtuous; but I am out of the road of rutting for ever.
translation: I'll do anything now, as long as its virtuous. I'm done with prostitutes forever.

original: Well, I had rather than twice the worth of her she had ne'er come here.
translation: I don't care what she's worth; I wish she had never come here.

original: Fie, fie upon her! she's able to freeze the god   Priapus, and undo a whole generation.
translation: Shame, shame on her! She could convince even the most  hot-blooded man  not to have sex.

original: We must   either get her ravished, or be rid of her.
translation: We either need to have someone sleep with her or get rid of her.

original: When she   should do for clients her fitment, and do me the   kindness of our profession, she has me her quirks,   her reasons, her master reasons, her prayers, her   knees;
translation: When she's supposed to be fulfilling her customers' desires (and giving me the profit), instead she's up to all her shenanigans: her excuses, her better excuses, her prayers, begging on her knees.

original: that she would make a puritan of the devil,   if he should cheapen a kiss of her.
translation: She could turn the devil himself into a  born-again Christian  if he so much as tried to kiss her.

original: 'Faith, I must ravish her, or she'll disfurnish us of all our cavaliers, and make our swearers priests.
translation: Well, I'll have to rape her, or she'll ruin all our customers, converting the evil-doers to good.

original: Now, the pox upon her green-sickness for me!
'Faith, there's no way to be rid on't but by the way to the pox. Here comes the Lord Lysimachus  disguised.
We should have both lord and lown, if the peevish baggage would but give way to customers.
translation: We could win him and his money over if the girl would just give in to customers.

original: How now! How a dozen of virginities?
translation: Hello! How much for a dozen virginities?

original: Now, the gods to-bless your honour!
translation: God bless you, sir.

original: I am glad to see your honour in good health.
translation: I'm glad to see you're healthy, sir.

original: You may so; 'tis the better for you that your   resorters stand upon sound legs.
translation: I'm sure you are— it's better for your business when your clients keep from getting sick!

original: How now!   wholesome iniquity have you that a man may deal   withal, and defy the surgeon?
translation: What new stock do you have here that might allow a man to enjoy his whores and keep the sexually-transmitted diseases at bay?

original: We have here one, sir, if she would—but there never came her like in Mytilene.
translation: We have one here, sir, if she would . . . but we've never had anyone like her in Mytilene.

original: If she'ld do the deed of darkness, thou wouldst say.
translation: If she would do the dirty, you mean.

original: Your honour knows what 'tis to say well enough.
translation: You're exactly right, sir.

original: Well, call forth, call forth.
translation: Well, bring her in, then!

original: For flesh and blood, sir, white and red, you shall see a rose; and she were a rose indeed, if she had but—
What, prithee?
translation: What did you say?

original: O, sir, I can be modest.
translation: Oh, sir, I can be quiet.

original: That dignifies the renown of a bawd, no less than it gives a good report to a number to be chaste.
Here comes that which grows to the stalk; never plucked yet, I can assure you.
translation: Here comes a fresh flower. Never been picked, I can assure you.

original: Is she not a fair creature?
translation: Isn't she pretty?

original: 'Faith, she would serve after a long voyage at sea. Well, there's for you: leave us.
translation: She's just what you want after a long voyage at sea.  Well, there you go. Leave us.

original: I beseech your honour, give me leave: a word, and I'll have done presently.
translation: Please, sir, let me speak with her first and then I'll leave you.

original: I beseech you, do.
translation: Please, do.

original: First, I would have you note, this is an honourable man.
translation: First, please note that he is an honorable man.

original: I desire to find him so, that I may worthily note him.
translation: I hope he proves himself so; then I can respect him.

original: Next, he's the governor of this country, and a man whom I am bound to.
translation: Second: he's the governor of this country, and I'm bound to serve him.

original: If he govern the country, you are bound to him indeed; but how honourable he is in that, I know not.
translation: If he governs the country, you are definitely bound to serve him. It's unclear how honorable he is in the act of governing, though.

original: Pray you, without any more virginal fencing, will you use him kindly? He will line your apron with gold.
translation: Please stop arguing with me. Will you do him well? He'll give you a lot of money.

original: What he will do graciously, I will thankfully receive.
translation: Whatever he gives courteously, I accept gratefully.

original: Ha' you done?
translation: Are you done?

original: My lord, she's not paced yet: you must take some pains to work her to your manage. Come, we will leave his honour and her together. Go thy ways.
translation: Sir, she hasn't been broken in yet; you'll need to work hard to make her obey.  Come on, we'll leave the two of them together. Go on, now.

original: Now, pretty one, how long have you been at this trade?
translation: So, pretty girl, how long have you been working in this business?

original: What trade, sir?
Why, I cannot name't but I shall offend.
translation: I can't say the name, or I'll offend you.

original: I cannot be offended with my trade. Please you to name  it.
translation: I can't be offended by the name of my business. Please say it.

original: How long have you been of this profession?
translation: How long have you been in this profession?

original: E'er since I can remember.
translation: Ever since I can remember.

original: Did you go to 't so young? Were you a gamester at five or at seven?
translation: Did you start that young? Were you a prostitute at the age of five or seven?

original: Earlier too, sir, if now I be one.
translation: Earlier that that, sir, if that's what I am now.

original: Why, the house you dwell in proclaims you to be a creature of sale.
translation: The place where you live proclaims you to be a prostitute.

original: Do you know this house to be a place of such resort, and will come into 't? I hear say you are of honourable parts, and are the governor of this place.
Why, hath your principal made known unto you who I am?
translation: Did your boss tell you who I am?

original: Who is my principal?
translation: Who is my boss?

original: Why, your herb-woman; she that sets seeds and roots   of shame and iniquity.
translation: The  B awd @ , the one that teaches you and facilitates your shame and wickedness.

original: O, you have heard something   of my power, and so stand aloof for more serious   wooing.
translation: All right, you've heard I'm powerful  and rich so you're playing hard to get.

original: But I protest to thee, pretty one, my   authority shall not see thee, or else look friendly   upon thee.
translation: I'll have you know, pretty girl, that once I see you, I'll pay you very well.

original: Come, bring me to some private place:   come, come.
translation: Come on, bring me to a private room. Come, come.

original: If you were born to honour, show it now;
translation: If you were born to power, sir, prove how honorable you are now.

original: If put upon you, make the judgment good   That thought you worthy of it.
translation: If you rose to power later, prove that those who thought you were honorable then made a good choice.

original: How's this? how's this? Some more; be sage.
translation: What? What? Say more, be clear.

original: For me,   That am a maid, though most ungentle fortune   Have placed me in this sty, where, since I came,   Diseases have been sold dearer than physic,
translation: I'm a virgin, although bad luck has landed me in this dump where, since I came people have paid more to get diseases than they would for medicine.

original: O, that the gods   Would set me free from this unhallow'd place,   Though they did change me to the meanest bird   That flies i' the purer air!
translation: Oh, may the gods set me free from this hellish place, even if it means changing me into a bird that flies through the pure air!

original: I did not think   Thou couldst have spoke so well; ne'er dream'd thou  couldst.
translation: I couldn't have imagined you could speak so well; I couldn't have dreamed it.

original: Had I brought hither a corrupted mind,   Thy speech had alter'd it.
translation: If I had had a dirty mind, your speech would have changed it.

original: Hold, here's gold for thee:   Persever in that clear way thou goest,   And the gods strengthen thee!
translation: Here, take this coin. Keep going on this virtuous path, and may the gods bless you!

original: The good gods preserve you!
translation: May the gods protect you!

original: For me, be you thoughten   That I came with no ill intent; for to me   The very doors and windows savour vilely.
translation: As for me: rest assured I had no bad intentions. Actually, this whole place is disgusting.

original: Fare thee well. Thou art a piece of virtue, and   I doubt not but thy training hath been noble.
translation: Goodbye. You are virtuous, and I have no doubt that you've had an aristocratic education.

original: Hold, here's more gold for thee.   A curse upon him, die he like a thief,   That robs thee of thy goodness!
translation: Here, here's more gold for you. Curse anyone who tries to force himself on you, may he die like a thief!

original: If thou dost   Hear from me, it shall be for thy good.
translation: If you ever hear from me again, it'll be for your benefit.

original: I beseech your honour, one piece for me.
translation: Please, sir, a coin for me?

original: Avaunt, thou damned door-keeper! Your house, but for this virgin that doth prop it, Would sink and overwhelm you. Away!
translation: Get out, you damned doorman! Without this virgin keeping it up, this whole house would collapse and bury you! Away!

original: How's this? We must take another course with you.
translation: What now? We'll have to try a different tactic with you.

original: If your peevish chastity, which is not worth a   breakfast in the cheapest country under the cope,   shall undo a whole household,
translation: Your worthless virginity—which isn't worth a cheap breakfast eaten in the night— isn't about to ruin this place;

original: let me be gelded like   a spaniel. Come your ways.
translation: I'd rather be neutered like a dog than see that happen. Come with me.

original: Whither would you have me?
translation: Where are you taking me?

original: I must have your maidenhead taken off, or the common   hangman shall execute it.
translation: I have to deflower you; otherwise you'll have to be killed.

original: Come your ways. We'll   have no more gentlemen driven away. Come your ways, I  say.
translation: Come with me. We can't have any more gentleman driven away. Come with me, I said!

original: How now! what's the matter?
translation: Hey, what's going on here?

original: Worse and worse, mistress; she has here spoken holy words to the Lord Lysimachus.
translation: Worse and worse, ma'am. She's preached some sermon to Lord Lysimachus.

original: O abominable!
translation: It's unthinkable!

original: She makes our profession as it were to stink afore the face of the gods.
translation: She's ruining the name of our profession.

original: Marry, hang her up for ever!
translation: For goodness' sake, have her hanged!

original: The nobleman would have dealt with her like a nobleman, and she sent him away as cold as a snowball; saying his prayers too.
translation: The nobleman would have done with her what a nobleman does, but she sent him away as cold as a snowball, and saying his prayers, too.

original: Boult, take her away; use her at thy pleasure: crack the glass of her virginity, and make the rest  malleable.
translation: Boult, take her away. Do whatever you like with her. Smash her virginity into pieces so we can mold the rest into whatever shape we want.

original: An if she were a thornier piece of ground than she is, she shall be ploughed.
translation: Even if she were uglier than she is, she'd have to be screwed.

original: Hark, hark, you gods!
translation: Gods, listen, help me!

original: She conjures: away with her! Would she had never   come within my doors! Marry, hang you! She's born   to undo us.
translation: She's praying; take her away! I wish she had never set foot in this house. Damn her! She's going to ruin us.

original: Will you not go the way of women-kind?   Marry, come up, my dish of chastity with rosemary and  bays!
translation: Don't you want to do what women do? Come up, my little  virgin pie  with rosemary and bay leaves!

original: Come, mistress; come your ways with me.
translation: Come on, missy, come with me.

original: Whither wilt thou have me?
translation: What are you going to do to me?

original: To take from you the jewel you hold so dear.
translation: Take away your most prized possession.

original: Prithee, tell me one thing first.
translation: Please, tell me one thing first.

original: Come now, your one thing.
translation: All right, what's your one thing?

original: What canst thou wish thine enemy to be?
translation: Who's the worst person you know?

original: Why, I could wish him to be my master, or rather, my  mistress.
translation: Probably the Pandar. Or the Bawd.

original: Neither of these are so bad as thou art,   Since they do better thee in their command.
translation: Neither of them is as bad as you; their jobs are better than yours.

original: Thou hold'st a place, for which the pained'st fiend   Of hell would not in reputation change:
translation: The worst demon in hell wouldn't trade places with you.

original: Thou art the damned doorkeeper to every   Coistrel that comes inquiring for his Tib;
translation: You're the damned doorman who lets in every vagabond that comes looking for his slut;

original: To the choleric fisting of every rogue   Thy ear is liable; thy food is such   As hath been belch'd on by infected lungs.
translation: every diseased person owes his misery to you. The very food you eat has been burped on by infected lungs.

original: What would you have me do? go to the wars, would   you?
translation: What do you want me to do? Fight in the war, huh?

original: where a man may serve seven years for the loss   of a leg, and have not money enough in the end to   buy him a wooden one?
translation: Where a man might serve seven years before he loses a leg, and then not have enough money to buy a wooden one?

original: Do any thing but this thou doest. Empty   Old receptacles, or common shores, of filth;
translation: Do anything but this. Empty trash cans, or clean up the beaches.

original: Serve by indenture to the common hangman:   Any of these ways are yet better than this;
translation: Work as an apprentice in the prison. Anything is better than this.

original: For what thou professest, a baboon, could he speak,   Would own a name too dear.
translation: What you do? If a baboon could speak, he would say your job is beneath him.

original: O, that the gods   Would safely deliver me from this place!   Here, here's gold for thee.
translation: I wish the gods would take me out of here safely! Here, take this gold coin.

original: If that thy master would gain by thee,   Proclaim that I can sing, weave, sew, and dance,   With other virtues, which I'll keep from boast:
translation: If your master is intent to make a profit from me, let him know I can sing, weave, sew, and dance, and more which I won't brag about.

original: And I will undertake all these to teach.   I doubt not but this populous city will   Yield many scholars.
translation: I'll hire myself out to teach all these. I have no doubt that I'll find plenty of students in the city.

original: But can you teach all this you speak of?
translation: Can you teach all those things?

original: Prove that I cannot, take me home again, And prostitute me to the basest groom That doth frequent your house.
translation: If it turns out that I can't, you can take me home and prostitute me to the lowest peasant that's a regular at your house.

original: Well, I will see what I can do for thee: if I can place thee, I will.
translation: Well, I'll see what I can do for you. If I can help you, I will.

original: But amongst honest women.
translation: I want to work among honest women.

original: 'Faith, my acquaintance lies little amongst them.   But since my master and mistress have bought you,   there's no going but by their consent:
translation: I don't know many of them, I'll tell you. But since my master and mistress have bought you, there's no way of going unless they consent.

original: therefore I   will make them acquainted with your purpose, and I   doubt not but I shall find them tractable enough.
translation: So I'll explain your plan to them; I'm sure they'll be willing.

original: Come, I'll do for thee what I can; come your ways.
translation: Come on, I'll do what I can for you.  Come with me.

original: [To the Sailor of Mytilene]   Where is lord Helicanus?   he can resolve you.   O, here he is.
translation: [To the Mytilene Sailor]  Where is Lord Helicanus? He can answer your questions. Oh, here he is.

original: Sir, there's a barge put off from Mytilene,   And in it is Lysimachus the governor,   Who craves to come aboard. What is your will?
translation: [To HELICANUS]  Sir, there's a boat that just came from Mytilene and Lysimachus, the governor, is in it, asking to come onboard. What should we do?

original: That he have his. Call up some gentlemen.
translation: Bring him aboard. And bring some gentlemen with you.

original: Ho, gentlemen! my lord calls.
translation: Hey, gentlemen! Helicanus is calling.

original: Doth your lordship call?
translation: Did you call, sir?

original: Gentlemen, there's some of worth would come aboard; I pray ye, greet them fairly.
translation: Gentlemen, there's some powerful people who want to come aboard. Please greet them warmly.

original: Sir, This is the man that can, in aught you would, Resolve you.
translation: Sir, this is the man who can answer whatever questions you may have.

original: Hail, reverend sir! the gods preserve you!
translation: Greetings, sir! May the gods bless you!

original: And you, sir, to outlive the age I am, And die as I would do.
translation: And you, sir. May you live longer than me and die an old man.

original: You wish me well.   Being on shore, honouring of Neptune's triumphs,   Seeing this goodly vessel ride before us,
translation: Thanks. I was on the shore, admiring  Neptune 's domain, when I saw your impressive ship sail toward us.

original: I made to it, to know of whence you are.
translation: I came out in my ship to find out where you've come from.

original: First, what is your place?
translation: First, who are you?

original: I am the governor of this place you lie before.
translation: I am the governor of the country you are now in.

original: Sir,   Our vessel is of Tyre, in it the king;
translation: Sir, our ship has come from Tyre, and the king is onboard.

original: A man who for this three months hath not spoken   To any one, nor taken sustenance   But to prorogue his grief.
translation: For the past three months he hasn't spoken to anyone and he's refused to eat anything more than what he needs to prolong his grieving.

original: Upon what ground is his distemperature?
translation: How did he get this way?

original: 'Twould be too tedious to repeat; But the main grief springs from the loss Of a beloved daughter and a wife.
translation: The story is too long to repeat, but the short version is that he lost his beloved daughter and his wife.

original: May we not see him?
translation: Can we see him?

original: You may; But bootless is your sight: he will not speak To any.
translation: You may, but it won't help. He won't speak to anyone.

original: Yet let me obtain my wish.
translation: Let me see him anyway.

original: Behold him.
translation: Here he is.

original: This was a goodly person, Till the disaster that, one mortal night, Drove him to this.
translation: He was a good man until the disaster that destroyed him in a single night.

original: Sir king, all hail! the gods preserve you! Hail, royal sir!
translation: Greetings, king! May the gods protect you. Greetings, sir!

original: It is in vain; he will not speak to you.
translation: It's no use; he won't speak to you.

original: Sir, We have a maid in Mytilene, I durst wager, Would win some words of him.
translation: Sir, there's a girl in Mytilene who could probably make him speak.

original: 'Tis well bethought.   She questionless with her sweet harmony   And other chosen attractions, would allure,   And make a battery through his deafen'd parts,   Which now are midway stopp'd:
translation: That's a good idea. Most likely, her beautiful voice and many other attractive qualities will allure him and get through to his deaf ears, though they're stopped up now.

original: She is all happy as the fairest of all,   And, with her fellow maids is now upon   The leafy shelter that abuts against   The island's side.
translation: She's the most beautiful girl there is. She's with her students now in the building surrounded by trees on the other side of the island.

original: Sure, all's effectless; yet nothing we'll omit   That bears recovery's name.
translation: It's probably useless, but we won't overlook anything that might help.

original: But, since your kindness   We have stretch'd thus far, let us beseech you   That for our gold we may provision have,   Wherein we are not destitute for want,   But weary for the staleness.
translation: And since we've taken advantage of your kindness so far, can I ask you if we could exchange our gold for food? We have some, but it's gone stale.

original: O, sir, a courtesy   Which if we should deny, the most just gods   For every graff would send a caterpillar,   And so afflict our province.
translation: Oh, sir, if I were to deny you that service, the most just gods would send a plague of caterpillars, one for every grain we didn't give, to afflict our country.

original: Yet once more   Let me entreat to know at large the cause   Of your king's sorrow.
translation: But let me ask again: can I hear the story of how your king came to be so sad?

original: Sit, sir, I will recount it to you: But, see, I am prevented.
translation: Sit, sir, and I'll tell you. But, as you can see, I'll be interrupted...

original: O, here is The lady that I sent for. Welcome, fair one! Is't not a goodly presence?
translation: Oh, here's the lady that I sent for. Hello, beautiful! Isn't she pretty?

original: She's a gallant lady.
translation: She's a noble lady.

original: She's such a one, that, were I well assured   Came of a gentle kind and noble stock,   I'ld wish no better choice, and think me rarely wed.
translation: She's so beautiful that, if I could only be assured she came from an aristocratic family and noble blood, I couldn't find a better choice, and would marry her.

original: Fair one, all goodness that consists in bounty   Expect even here, where is a kingly patient:
translation: Beautiful girl, you can expect to be rewarded generously for helping the sick king here.

original: If that thy prosperous and artificial feat   Can draw him but to answer thee in aught,   Thy sacred physic shall receive such pay   As thy desires can wish.
translation: If your artistic talents are successful in getting him to respond to you in anything, we'll pay you anything you want for the healing.

original: Sir, I will use   My utmost skill in his recovery,
translation: Sir, I'll use all the skills I have to help him,

original: provided   That none but I and my companion maid   Be suffer'd to come near him.
translation: as long as no one but me and my maid are allowed to come near him.

original: Come, let us leave her; And the gods make her prosperous!
translation: Come, let's leave her. May the gods help her!

original: Mark'd he your music?
translation: Did he listen to your music?

original: No, nor look'd on us.
translation: No, and he didn't look at us.

original: See, she will speak to him.
translation: See, she's going to speak to him.

original: Hail, sir! my lord, lend ear.
translation: Hello, sir! Sir, will you listen to me?

original: Hum, ha!
translation: Hmm, ha!

original: I am a maid,   My lord, that ne'er before invited eyes,   But have been gazed on like a comet:
translation: I'm a virgin, sir, and though I've never asked for anyone's attention, I've had a lot of people stare at me (as though I were a shooting star)!

original: she speaks,   My lord, that, may be, hath endured a grief   Might equal yours, if both were justly weigh'd.
translation: I'm speaking to you, sir, because I think I may have experienced grief that, if we compared, might equal yours.

original: Though wayward fortune did malign my state,   My derivation was from ancestors   Who stood equivalent with mighty kings:
translation: Though I've been unlucky to end up where I am now, I'm descended from ancestors who were the equivalent of powerful kings.

original: But time hath rooted out my parentage,   And to the world and awkward casualties   Bound me in servitude.
translation: I've been robbed of my inheritance from my parents, and over the course of time have been forced to serve the world and its uncomfortable institutions.

original: [Aside]   I will desist;   But there is something glows upon my cheek,   And whispers in mine ear, 'Go not till he speak.'
translation: [To herself]  I should stop. But there's something that warms my cheek, a little voice inside me telling me, "Keep going until he says something."

original: My fortunes—parentage—good parentage— To equal mine!—was it not thus? what say you?
translation: My luck . . . parents . . . good parents . . . like me! Was it really? What did you say?

original: I said, my lord, if you did know my parentage, You would not do me violence.
translation: I said, sir, that if you knew who my parents were, you wouldn't hurt me.

original: I do think so. Pray you, turn your eyes upon me. You are like something that—What country-woman? Here of these shores?
translation: I believe you. Please, look at me. You remind me of someone . . . where are you from? From this country?

original: No, nor of any shores: Yet I was mortally brought forth, and am No other than I appear.
translation: No, I wasn't born in any country. And yet I was born, and am exactly what I seem.

original: I am great with woe, and shall deliver weeping.   My dearest wife was like this maid, and such a one   My daughter might have been:
translation: I'm  so upset;  I'm about to start crying. My wife looked just like this girl, and my daughter might have looked like her if she had survived:

original: my queen's square brows;   Her stature to an inch; as wand-like straight;   As silver-voiced; her eyes as jewel-like   And cased as richly; in pace another Juno;
translation: she has my wife's thick eyebrows, her exact height, her straight posture, her beautiful voice, her  sparkling eyes framed in rich eyelashes , with a walk as graceful as  Juno's ,

original: Who starves the ears she feeds, and makes them hungry,   The more she gives them speech. Where do you live?
translation: and a voice that makes people hungry to hear her speak. Where do you live?

original: Where I am but a stranger: from the deck You may discern the place.
translation: I'm just a stranger here: you can see where I live from the deck of this boat.

original: Where were you bred? And how achieved you these endowments, which You make more rich to owe?
translation: Where were you born? And how did you achieve all these accomplishments?

original: If I should tell my history, it would seem Like lies disdain'd in the reporting.
translation: If I told you my story, you would think I was lying.

original: Prithee, speak:   Falseness cannot come from thee; for thou look'st   Modest as Justice, and thou seem'st a palace   For the crown'd Truth to dwell in:
translation: Please, speak. You can't tell a lie; you look like the embodiment of Justice, like the queen of Truth.

original: I will   believe thee,   And make my senses credit thy relation   To points that seem impossible; for thou look'st   Like one I loved indeed.
translation: I will believe you, even if you say things that seem impossible, because you look like someone I used to love.

original: What were thy friends?   Didst thou not say, when I did push thee back—   Which was when I perceived thee—   that thou camest   From good descending?
translation: Who was your family? Didn't you say, when I pushed you back, when I first looked at you, that you came from a good family?

original: So indeed I did.
translation: Yes, I did.

original: Report thy parentage.
translation: Tell me who your parents were.

original: I think thou said'st   Thou hadst been toss'd from wrong to injury,   And that thou thought'st thy griefs might equal mine,   If both were open'd.
translation: I think you said you'd been wronged and hurt in the past, and that you thought you had suffered as much as I had (if the stories were both told).

original: Some such thing I said, and said no more but what my thoughts Did warrant me was likely.
translation: I said something like that, but I only said what I thought might be true.

original: Tell thy story;   If thine consider'd prove the thousandth part   Of my endurance, thou art a man, and I   Have suffer'd like a girl:
translation: Tell your story; if you've experienced one thousandth of what I have, you're a man and I've suffered like a girl.

original: yet thou dost look   Like Patience gazing on kings' graves, and smiling   Extremity out of act. What were thy friends?
translation: You look patient in the  face of death ; you're smiling as if nothing had happened! Who was your family?

original: How lost thou them? Thy name, my most kind virgin?   Recount, I do beseech thee: come, sit by me.
translation: How did you lose them? What is your name, friendly virgin? Please, tell me, I'm begging you. Come sit by me.

original: My name is Marina.
translation: My name is Marina.

original: O, I am mock'd, And thou by some incensed god sent hither To make the world to laugh at me.
translation: This is a joke. Some angry god has sent you here to make the world laugh at me.

original: Patience, good sir, Or here I'll cease.
translation: Sir, please listen, or I'll stop here.

original: Nay, I'll be patient. Thou little know'st how thou dost startle me, To call thyself Marina.
translation: I'll listen. You have no idea how much you've startled me by calling yourself "Marina."

original: The name Was given me by one that had some power, My father, and a king.
translation: The name was given to me by a powerful person: my father, who was a king.

original: How! a king's daughter? And call'd Marina?
translation: What? You're a king's daughter named Marina?

original: You said you would believe me; But, not to be a troubler of your peace, I will end here.
translation: You said you would believe me. I won't bother you anymore; I'll stop there.

original: But are you flesh and blood?   Have you a working pulse? and are no fairy?
translation: Are you flesh and blood? Is your heart beating? You're not a ghost?

original: Motion! Well; speak on. Where were you born?   And wherefore call'd Marina?
translation: You're alive! Well, keep talking. Where were you born? And why were you called Marina?

original: Call'd Marina For I was born at sea.
translation: I was called Marina because I was born at sea.

original: At sea! what mother?
translation: At sea! Who was your mother?

original: My mother was the daughter of a king;   Who died the minute I was born,
translation: My mother was the daughter of a king, and she died as soon as I was born.

original: As my good nurse Lychorida hath oft   Deliver'd weeping.
translation: My nurse, Lychorida, told me the story many times, crying.

original: O, stop there a little!
translation: Oh, wait a minute!

original: [Aside]   This is the rarest dream that e'er dull sleep   Did mock sad fools withal: this cannot be:   My daughter's buried.
translation: [To himself]  This is the strangest dream that a poor idiot ever had. This can't be true; my daughter is dead.

original: Well: where were you bred?   I'll hear you more, to the bottom of your story,   And never interrupt you.
translation: [To MARINA]  Well, where were you born? I'll listen to you again, to the whole story, and won't interrupt you anymore.

original: You scorn: believe me, 'twere best I did give o'er.
translation: You're making fun of me. Believe me; it's best if I stop.

original: I will believe you by the syllable Of what you shall deliver. Yet, give me leave: How came you in these parts? where were you bred?
translation: I'll believe every word you say. But let me ask: how did you get here? Where were you born?

original: The king my father did in Tarsus leave me;   Till cruel Cleon, with his wicked wife,   Did seek to murder me:
translation: My father, the king, left me in Tarsus until the king, Cleon, and his evil wife tried to murder me.

original: and having woo'd   A villain to attempt it, who having drawn to do't,   A crew of pirates came and rescued me;   Brought me to Mytilene.
But, good sir,   Whither will you have me? Why do you weep?
translation: Sir, did I say something wrong? Why are you crying?

original: It may be,   You think me an impostor: no, good faith;   I am the daughter to King Pericles,   If good King Pericles be.
translation: Maybe you think I'm a fake, but I'm not: I'm good King Pericles's daughter, if good King Pericles is still alive.

original: Ho, Helicanus!
translation: Hey, Helicanus!

original: Calls my lord?
translation: Did you call, sir?

original: Thou art a grave and noble counsellor,   Most wise in general:
translation: You're a serious, noble advisor, and wise about many different things:

original: tell me, if thou canst,   What this maid is, or what is like to be,   That thus hath made me weep?
translation: tell me, if you can, what this girl is, or is supposed to be, that she's made me cry so much?

original: I know not; but Here is the regent, sir, of Mytilene Speaks nobly of her.
translation: I don't know, but here's the governor of Mytilene, sir, and he speaks highly of her.

original: She would never tell Her parentage; being demanded that, She would sit still and weep.
translation: She would never tell me who her parents were. Whenever I asked, she would sit still and weep.

original: O Helicanus, strike me, honour'd sir;   Give me a gash, put me to present pain;
translation: Oh, Helicanus, pinch me! Hit me, make me feel some pain,

original: Lest this great sea of joys rushing upon me   O'erbear the shores of my mortality,   And drown me with their sweetness   .
translation: or this  great sea  of happiness will overwhelm me and kill me!

original: O, come hither,   Thou that beget'st him that did thee beget;   Thou that wast born at sea, buried at Tarsus,   And found at sea again!
translation: [To MARINA]  Oh come here; I gave birth to you, but finding you makes me feel like I'm  reborn . You were born at sea, buried in Tarsus, and found at sea again!

original: O Helicanus,   Down on thy knees, thank the holy gods as loud   As thunder threatens us: this is Marina.
translation: [To HELICANUS]  Oh, Helicanus, kneel and thank the gods in a voice louder than the storm: this is Marina.

original: What was thy mother's name? tell me but that,   For truth can never be confirm'd enough,   Though doubts did ever sleep.
translation: [To MARINA]  What was your mother's name? Tell me that. The truth can never be confirmed enough, even if I have no doubts.

original: First, sir, I pray, What is your title?
translation: First, sir, please: who are you?

original: I am Pericles of Tyre: but tell me now   My drown'd queen's name, as in the rest you said   Thou hast been godlike perfect,
translation: I am Pericles of Tyre, but tell me my drowned wife's name. Everything you've said has been completely perfect. If you get this right,

original: The heir of kingdoms and another like   To Pericles thy father.
translation: you're the heir to two kingdoms and to me, your father, Pericles.

original: Is it no more to be your daughter than   To say my mother's name was Thaisa?
translation: Will it prove I'm your daughter if I say my mother's name was Thaisa?

original: Thaisa was my mother, who did end   The minute I began.
translation: Thaisa was my mother, and she died as soon as I was born.

original: Now, blessing on thee! rise; thou art my child.   Give me fresh garments. Mine own, Helicanus;
translation: Now bless you! Get up; you are my child. Bring me fresh clothes. She's my daughter, Helicanus.

original: She is not dead at Tarsus, as she should have been,   By savage Cleon:
translation: She's wasn't killed by Cleon back in Tarsus like she should have been.

original: she shall tell thee all;   When thou shalt kneel, and justify in knowledge   She is thy very princess. Who is this?
translation: She can tell you everything, but first kneel and acknowledge her as your princess. Who is this?

original: Sir, 'tis the governor of Mytilene, Who, hearing of your melancholy state, Did come to see you.
translation: Sir, it's the governor of Mytilene. He heard how melancholy you were and came to see you.

original: I embrace you.   Give me my robes. I am wild in my beholding.   O heavens bless my girl!
translation: I'll give you a hug. Give me my clothes. I'm overwhelmed with what I've seen. May the heavens bless my girl!

original: But, hark, what music?   Tell Helicanus, my Marina, tell him   O'er, point by point, for yet he seems to doubt,   How sure you are my daughter.
translation: But listen: what's that music? Tell Helicanus, my Marina, tell him the whole thing, point by point, because he still seems unsure— tell him that you're my daughter.

original: But, what music?
translation: But what's that music?

original: My lord, I hear none.
translation: Sir, I can't hear anything.

original: None! The music of the spheres! List, my Marina.
It is not good to cross him; give him way.
translation: It's not good to contradict him; let him go on.

original: Rarest sounds! Do ye not hear?
translation: Strange sounds! Can't you hear?

original: My lord, I hear.
translation: Sir, I hear.

original: Most heavenly music! It nips me unto listening, and thick slumber Hangs upon mine eyes: let me rest.
translation: The most heavenly music! I can't stop listening; and it's making me sleepy. Let me rest.

original: A pillow for his head:   So, leave him all.
translation: Get a pillow for his head. Let's all leave him.

original: Well, my companion friends,   If this but answer to my just belief,   I'll well remember you.
translation: Well, friends, if all this is true, I'll never forget you.

original: My temple stands in Ephesus: hie thee thither,   And do upon mine altar sacrifice.
translation: My temple is in Ephesus. Go there and make a sacrifice at my altar.

original: There, when my maiden priests are met together,   Before the people all,   Reveal how thou at sea didst lose thy wife:
translation: In front of the virgin nuns and people there, reveal the story of how you lost your wife at sea.

original: To mourn thy crosses, with thy daughter's, call   And give them repetition to the life.   Or perform my bidding, or thou livest in woe;
translation: Weep for your grief, and your daughter's. Bring the stories to life by repeating them. Do what I say, or you'll live a cursed life.

original: Do it, and happy; by my silver bow!   Awake, and tell thy dream.
translation: If you do it, you'll be happy, I'll make sure of it! Now wake up and tell about your dream.

original: Celestial Dian, goddess argentine, I will obey thee. Helicanus!
translation: Heavenly Diana, silver goddess, I will obey you. Helicanus!

original: Sir?
translation: Sir?

original: My purpose was for Tarsus, there to strike   The inhospitable Cleon; but I am   For other service first:
translation: I had planned to go to Tarsus and wage war on Cleon, but I have to do something else first.

original: toward Ephesus   Turn our blown sails; eftsoons I'll tell thee why.
translation: Turn the sails toward Ephesus. I'll tell you why soon.

original: [To LYSIMACHUS]   Shall we refresh us, sir, upon your shore,   And give you gold for such provision   As our intents will need?
